@@ -0,0 +1,351 @@
+# Elderly Fall Detection System
+
+A real-time, camera-only fall detection system that tracks people with skeleton pose estimation and combines a learned temporal classifier with a deterministic geometric scoring system to decide when someone has fallen and is down. Built for elderly care facilities, hospitals, and smart-home monitoring — no wearable device required.
+
+---
+
+## Why This Matters
+
+| The Problem | The Impact |
+|-------------|-----------|
+| **684,000** older adults die from falls globally each year (WHO) | Falls are the **#1 cause of injury death** among people aged 65+ |
+| **37.3 million** falls per year are severe enough to require medical attention | Average hospital cost per fall: **$35,000+** |
+| **95% of hip fractures** are caused by falling | A person lying on the floor for **>1 hour** has a 50% mortality rate within 6 months |
+
+The critical factor is response time. This system detects a fall and a subsequent "down" state automatically, from ordinary video, so help can be dispatched faster.
+
+---
+
+## How It Works
+
+Every tracked person is scored by **two independent evidence sources** each frame, which are then fused and passed through a per-track state machine before anything is reported:
+
+```
+Video Frame
+    |
+    v
+[1] YOLO11-Pose + BoT-SORT  -->  Detect people, 17 skeleton keypoints, persistent track IDs
+    |                              (+ ROI re-detection / rotation search to recover lost tracks)
+    v
+    +-------------------------------+-------------------------------+
+    |                                                                |
+    v                                                                v
+[2a] 5-feature LSTM classifier                     [2b] Deterministic "Mandown" scorer
+     30-frame sliding window -->                        posture/geometry features, per-camera
+     P(Normal / Falling / Fallen)                        scene + person-size calibration, optional
+     (pretrained, unchanged input contract)               monocular 2D->3D pose lifting for
+                                                           falls toward/away from the camera
+    |                                                                |
+    +-------------------------------+-------------------------------+
+                                     v
+                     [3] Evidence Fusion  -->  weighted combination + override rules
+                                     |          (a single very strong signal can be enough;
+                                     |           the two sources check each other otherwise)
+                                     v
+                     [4] Per-track State Machine  -->  NORMAL / POSSIBLE_MANDOWN / MANDOWN
+                                     |                  (hysteresis: sustained streaks, not
+                                     |                   single frames, drive transitions)
+                                     v
+                 Annotated Video + JSON Event Log + Event Screenshots
+```
+
+The LSTM is not the sole authority — it is one of two evidence sources that are fused together, so a confident-but-wrong classifier can be overruled by strong geometric evidence (and vice versa) before a fall is confirmed.
+

+

+

+---
+
+## Model Performance (LSTM classifier)
+
+The 5-feature LSTM is one of the two fused evidence sources; these are its standalone metrics on held-out test data.
+
+| Metric | Score |
+|--------|-------|
+| **Accuracy** | 98.2% |
+| **Macro F1** | 97.8% |
+| **Macro AUC** | 0.998 |
+
+### Per-Class Performance
+
+![Per-Class Metrics](docs/images/per_class_metrics.png)
+
+| Class | Precision | Recall | F1-Score | AUC |
+|-------|-----------|--------|----------|-----|
+| **Normal** | 98.6% | 98.7% | 98.6% | 0.998 |
+| **Falling** | 99.7% | 95.3% | 97.4% | 0.998 |
+| **Fallen** | 95.3% | 99.4% | 97.3% | 0.999 |
+
+### Confusion Matrix
+
+![Confusion Matrix](docs/images/confusion_matrix.png)
+
+### ROC Curves
+
+![ROC Curves](docs/images/roc_curves.png)
+
+### Training Progress
+
+![Training Curves](docs/images/training_curves.png)
+
+*2-layer LSTM, 128 hidden units, dropout=0.3, LayerNorm — 201,859 parameters. Converged within 38 epochs.*
+
+---
+
+## Detection States
+
+Each tracked person's state machine reports one of three tiers, displayed using the original vocabulary:
+
+| Internal Tier | Displayed As | Description |
+|----------------|--------------|-------------|
+| `NORMAL` | **NORMAL** (green) | Standing, walking, sitting, or otherwise upright/active |
+| `POSSIBLE_MANDOWN` | **FALLING** (red, alert) | Fusion evidence trending toward down, not yet confirmed |
+| `MANDOWN` | **FALLEN** (orange, timer) | Confirmed down; state is sticky until a sustained recovery streak |
+
+Transitions require sustained evidence over multiple frames (hysteresis), not a single frame's reading, which keeps brief occlusions or noisy detections from flipping the state.
+
+---
+
+## Tech Stack
+
+| Component | Technology | Purpose |
+|-----------|-----------|---------|
+| **Pose Estimation** | YOLO11-Pose (Ultralytics) | Person detection + 17 skeleton keypoints |
+| **Tracking** | BoT-SORT (+ custom ROI re-detection) | Multi-person tracking, recovers tracks lost to occlusion |
+| **Temporal Classifier** | LSTM (PyTorch) | Classifies 30-frame windows of 5 base features |
+| **Geometric Scorer** | Custom Python (`feature_mandown.py`) | Deterministic down/fallen scoring from richer posture/geometry features |
+| **3D Lifting (optional)** | MediaPipe BlazePose | Monocular 2D→3D pose lifting for falls along the camera's depth axis |
+| **Evidence Fusion** | Custom Python (`fusion.py`) | Weighted combination + override rules across both evidence sources |
+| **Temporal Hysteresis** | Custom Python (`state_machine.py`) | Per-track state machine (NORMAL / POSSIBLE_MANDOWN / MANDOWN) |
+| **Per-Camera Calibration** | Custom Python (`scene_profile.py`, `person_size_stats.py`) | Learns expected standing size/floor region per camera at runtime |
+| **Video I/O** | OpenCV | Read/write video files with annotation overlays |
+
+---
+
+## Dataset (LSTM training data)
+
+| Source | Videos | Type | Content |
+|--------|--------|------|---------|
+| **UR Fall Detection** | 70 | Image sequences | 30 falls + 40 daily activities (indoor, Kinect) |
+| **Le2i Fall Dataset** | 140 | Video files | 70 falls + 70 normal (4 room types, CCTV) |
+| **Synthetic** | — | Generated | 3,000 feature sequences with realistic fall patterns |
+
+| Split | Samples |
+|-------|---------|
+| Train | 14,001 |
+| Validation | 1,750 |
+| Test | 1,751 |
+| **Total** | **17,502** |
+
+---
+
+## Quick Start
+
+### Installation
+
+```bash
+git clone <repo-url>
+cd fall-detection-vison
+
+python3 -m venv .venv
+source .venv/bin/activate
+
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+YOLO pose/detection weights (`yolo11n.pt`, `yolo11s-pose.pt`, etc.) and the trained LSTM checkpoint (`models/checkpoints/best.pth`) are not tracked in git — the YOLO weights are downloaded automatically by Ultralytics on first run; the LSTM checkpoint must be trained (`src/train.py`) or obtained separately.
+
+### Run on a video file
+
+Drop the video in `input/` and run with just its filename — the annotated video and JSON log are written to `output/` automatically:
+
+```bash
+python detect_falls.py --input your_video.mp4
+# -> output/your_video.mp4, output/your_video_events.json
+```
+
+Explicit paths still work if you want to override the defaults:
+
+```bash
+python detect_falls.py \
+    --input your_video.mp4 \
+    --output result.mp4 \
+    --json-log events.json
+```
+
+### Run on a live RTSP camera or webcam
+
+```bash
+python detect_falls.py --input rtsp://user:pass@camera-ip/stream
+# or a local webcam:
+python detect_falls.py --input 0
+```
+
+This opens a real-time preview window with the same skeleton/box/alert overlays as video mode, but **no inference video is written** — only a screenshot per confirmed fall event, saved to `events/`. Stop with `q`/Esc in the preview window or Ctrl+C. Use `--no-display` to run headless (events still save).
+
+### CLI Options
+
+| Argument | Default | Description |
+|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `--input` / `-i` | (required) | Video file (checked in `input/` if not found as given), RTSP/HTTP stream URL, or webcam index |
+| `--output` / `-o` | `output/<name>.mp4` | Output annotated video path (video files only) |
+| `--json-log` / `-j` | `output/<name>_events.json` | JSON event log output path |
+| `--events-dir` | `events` | Folder where fall event screenshots are saved |
+| `--no-display` | off | For live streams: skip the preview window |
+| `--model` | `models/checkpoints/best.pth` | LSTM model checkpoint |
+| `--yolo-model` | `yolo11s-pose.pt` | YOLO pose model |
+| `--imgsz` | `1280` | YOLO inference resolution (long side, pixels) |
+| `--confidence` | `0.40` | Fall confidence threshold |
+| `--cooldown` | `90` | Cooldown frames between alerts |
+| `--device` | auto | `cuda` or `cpu` |
+
+### Output
+
+1. **Annotated video** (video files only) — skeletons, bounding boxes, fall alert banner, status bar
+2. **JSON event log** — structured data with timestamps, confidence scores, track IDs, and the saved screenshot path
+3. **Event screenshots** — saved to `events/` the moment a tracked person is classified as MANDOWN, once per event
+
+```json
+{
+  "events": [
+    {
+      "type": "fall",
+      "track_id": 1,
+      "start_frame": 114,
+      "timestamp_start": "00:00:04.750",
+      "confidence": 0.84,
+      "screenshot_path": "events/fall_track1_20260824_154735_956.jpg"
+    }
+  ],
+  "summary": {
+    "total_falls": 1,
+    "persons_tracked": 5
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Running the tests
+
+```bash
+pytest
+```
+
+275 tests across 17 files cover feature extraction, the LSTM-facing pipeline, the geometric scorer, fusion rules, the state machine, per-camera calibration, video I/O, and event deduplication.
+
+---
+
+## Project Structure
+
+```
+fall-detection-vison/
+├── detect_falls.py                # CLI entry point
+├── configs/

+
+---
+
+## Key Features
+
+- **No wearable device required** — works with any standard camera
+- **Multi-person tracking** — monitors multiple people simultaneously with persistent IDs
+- **Dual evidence detection** — a learned classifier and a deterministic geometric scorer check each other before confirming a fall
+- **Per-camera auto-calibration** — learns expected standing size and floor region at runtime, no manual setup per camera
+- **Depth-axis fall coverage** — optional 2D→3D pose lifting catches falls toward/away from the camera that flat 2D angles miss
+- **Persistent fall alerts** — MANDOWN state stays active with a duration timer until a sustained recovery streak is seen
+- **Resolution adaptive** — overlays scale automatically from 720p to 4K
+- **Low false positives** — breakdancing, yoga, sitting on the floor correctly classified as normal
+- **JSON event logging** — structured output for integration with alert systems
+- **Track recovery** — ROI re-detection and rotation search recover tracks BoT-SORT loses to occlusion
+
+---
+
+## Limitations & Future Work
+
+### Current Limitations
+- Trained primarily on indoor/surveillance-style footage — performance may vary in unusual environments
+- Requires several seconds of tracking before per-camera calibration and classification are fully confident
+- Very small persons (far from camera) may have noisy keypoint estimates
+- No web UI yet — `streamlit`/`gradio`/`fastapi` are listed in `requirements.txt` for a planned UI, but `app/` is currently an empty stub; the CLI is the only working entry point
+
+### Future Improvements
+- Build out the web UI (Streamlit/Gradio) referenced by the `app/` stub
+- Fine-tune on domain-specific data (specific camera angles, environments)
+- Deploy as an edge application (an ONNX + `simple_tracker.py` path already exists in `scripts/edge_inference.py`)
+- Alert integration (SMS, email, alarm system)
+
+---

+# BoT-SORT Tracker Configuration for Fall Detection
+# Optimized for indoor elderly monitoring scenarios
+
+tracker_type: botsort
+
+# Tracking thresholds
+track_high_thresh: 0.5      # High confidence detection threshold
+track_low_thresh: 0.1       # Low confidence detection threshold
+new_track_thresh: 0.6       # Threshold for creating new tracks
+track_buffer: 60            # Frames to keep lost tracks (2s at 30fps)
+match_thresh: 0.8           # Matching threshold for associations
+fuse_score: true            # Fuse detection score with motion/IoU for matching
+
+# BoT-SORT specific
+gmc_method: none            # Global motion compensation disabled (static camera; sparseOptFlow was
+                             # intermittently crashing OpenCV's LK optical flow and falling back anyway)
+proximity_thresh: 0.5       # Spatial proximity threshold
+appearance_thresh: 0.25     # Appearance similarity threshold
+
+# Re-ID
+with_reid: false            # Disable ReID for speed
+model: auto                 # ReID model (auto = use detector features)

+# Central configuration for the Mandown detection algorithmic core.
+# LSTM/detector model paths and BoT-SORT tracker settings are configured
+# elsewhere (FallDetectionPipeline constructor args, configs/botsort.yaml).
+# This file holds the thresholds/weights for the components added on top
+# of the existing YOLO-pose + LSTM pipeline: scene normalization, rolling
+# person-size stats, feature-based Mandown scoring, evidence fusion, and
+# the temporal state machine.
+
+# Reliability filters applied before a detection is used for calibration
+# (scene profile / rolling person-size stats). Keeps corrupted/truncated/
+# low-confidence boxes out of the statistics.
+calibration:
+  min_keypoint_confidence: 0.5      # mean keypoint confidence to trust a detection
+  min_critical_keypoints: 4         # of {shoulders, hips, ankles} (6 total) required visible
+  frame_edge_margin_px: 4           # bbox within this many px of frame border = truncated, rejected
+  min_aspect_ratio_for_standing: 0.15
+  max_aspect_ratio_for_standing: 0.75  # only "tall/narrow" boxes count as standing-like samples
+  min_samples_for_confidence: 15    # below this, scene/size stats are "unavailable"
+  full_confidence_samples: 50       # at/above this many samples, calibration confidence = 1.0
+
+# Rolling person-size statistics (per camera). 30 samples, refreshed in
+# stride-10 batches (see RollingPersonSizeStats) -- decided against real
+# RTSP deployment: fast enough to calibrate a live camera's average person
+# height within the first couple dozen reliable detections.
+rolling_size:
+  window_size: 30
+  update_stride: 10
+  outlier_reject_iqr_multiplier: 2.5  # reject samples beyond median +/- k*IQR when computing stats
+  full_confidence_samples: 30         # own saturation point -- reaches confidence=1.0 once the window fills
+
+# Direct feature-based Mandown scoring weights (Phase 6).
+# Each sub-score is in [0, 1]; combined into `down_score`.
+feature_mandown:
+  motion_window_frames: 15           # recent-history window for fall-motion / angle-change scoring
+  persistence_window_frames: 45      # ~1.5s at 30fps, window for persistence_score
+  weights:
+    down_score: 0.40
+    fall_motion_score: 0.20
+    floor_proximity_score: 0.20
+    persistence_score: 0.10
+    floor_contact_score: 0.10        # absolute floor-band evidence; contributes 0 until scene is calibrated
+  # Sigmoid steepness/midpoints for continuous (non hard-threshold) cue mapping.
+  # cog_height and body-relative-height cues are normalized 0-1 before this.
+  sigmoid_steepness: 10.0
+  # V4: orientation-invariant lying geometry (diagonal lying / side-lying with
+  # bent knees). torso_angle-based down/floor-proximity cues are reshaped
+  # around this boundary instead of climbing linearly to 90 deg; body_axis_angle
+  # (long-baseline head->ankle-mid) may only corroborate -- not override -- a
+  # torso reading that already shows this much lean, and even then only
+  # partially. See src/config.py::OrientationConfig for the full rationale.
+  orientation:
+    upright_boundary: 0.40
+    boundary_steepness: 10.0  # matches this section's own sigmoid_steepness default above
+    corroboration_floor: 0.5   # axis may only corroborate once torso itself already clears upright_boundary
+    corroboration_weight: 0.5
+  # V4.2: a person who falls toward/away from the camera (foreshortened --
+  # angle-based cues above stay near "upright" since the fall is along the
+  # depth axis, not across the image plane) is invisible to torso/axis
+  # angles. body_height_norm (bbox height vs. calibrated expected standing
+  # height at this image row) doesn't depend on fall direction, so a strong
+  # calibrated shortfall directly corroborates down_score/floor_proximity_score
+  # instead of being diluted at a fixed 20% weight. Only ever activates on a
+  # real calibrated shortfall -- defaults to a neutral, non-triggering
+  # reading whenever scene calibration is unavailable.
+  height_collapse:
+    corroboration_floor: 0.5
+    # 0.75, not 0.5 (the value reused from OrientationConfig at first draft)
+    # -- calibrated separately: at 0.5 a genuine foreshortened fall's
+    # down_score only reached ~0.46-0.60, not enough headroom for the
+    # confirmed_mandown_floor_proximity_floor path below to matter in
+    # practice. Verified safe against the same adversarial occluded-seated
+    # fixture used to calibrate OrientationConfig's 0.5.
+    corroboration_weight: 0.75
+
+# V2: kneeling/sitting discrimination (Phase 9). A bent leg (kneeling, sitting)
+# should never read as "lying" even when the torso pitches forward and the
+# head/knee vertical span collapses like it does in true lying.
+kneeling:
+  extension_ratio_threshold: 0.85    # leg_extension_ratio below this reads as "bent" (kneeling/sitting)
+  sigmoid_steepness: 12.0
+  upright_gate_power: 1.0            # penalty is scaled by (1 - torso_angle) ** this — weakens as the
+                                      # torso pitches toward horizontal (true lying), but...
+  min_gate: 0.35                     # ...never fully vanishes for a moderately forward-leaning
+                                      # kneeling posture, but this floor itself fades out above...
+  extreme_lying_torso_angle: 0.9     # ...this torso_angle — a genuinely flat lying-with-bent-knee
+                                      # posture must not be floored the same as forward-leaning kneeling
+  # V3: occlusion handling (Phase 6) — when legs aren't confidently visible,
+  # leg_extension_ratio's neutral default must not be read as "confirmed
+  # extended". Falls back to a leg-independent torso-upright signal instead.
+  leg_evidence_quality_threshold: 0.5  # below this, legs are treated as occluded/unknown
+  torso_upright_gap_threshold: 0.25    # head-to-hip normalized gap above which the torso
+                                        # alone reads as upright, regardless of unseen legs
+  # V4.6: real RTSP miss -- a person fallen toward the camera with legs
+  # unevidenced was never flagged because upright_gate above reads
+  # torso_angle~0 the same for genuine upright/kneeling AND a foreshortened
+  # fall. Corroborate with height_collapse_cue (calibrated body_height_norm,
+  # never torso angle): only relent when torso is confirmed near-zero AND
+  # height evidence strongly confirms genuine collapse. See
+  # src/config.py::KneelingConfig for the measured real-camera numbers.
+  foreshortened_relent_torso_angle_ceiling: 0.2
+  foreshortened_relent_height_collapse_floor: 0.7
+  # V4.8: monocular 2D->3D pose lifting (src/pose_3d.py) gives a DIRECT,
+  # camera-calibration-independent measurement of real torso orientation.
+  # Crouching (torso vertical in 3D despite a shortened observed bbox)
+  # should read LOW here, unlike the height_collapse proxy above which
+  # can't tell it apart from genuine lying -- a conservative floor (~50
+  # deg from vertical) with margin above ordinary kneeling/crouching. See
+  # src/config.py::KneelingConfig for the full rationale.
+  pose3d_lying_relent_floor: 0.55
+
+# V2: floor-region reasoning (Phase 5) — a rolling estimate of the image band
+# where this camera's tracked people actually touch the ground (from ankle
+# y-positions), independent of the perspective-height regression. Marked
+# unavailable until enough reliable samples exist.
+floor_region:
+  min_samples_for_confidence: 15
+  full_confidence_samples: 50
+  band_half_width_ratio: 0.5         # half-width of the floor band = this * ankle-y IQR
+
+# V4: event-level deduplication (Phase 12) — the same physical downed person
+# can fragment across two simultaneously-active BoT-SORT track IDs (real case:
+# man_down_c08.mp4). A new event whose bbox substantially overlaps an already-
+# active event's most recent bbox is treated as the same physical event, not
+# a second alert. Two genuinely different people rarely sustain this much
+# overlap on a new event's very first frame.
+event_dedup:
+  iou_threshold: 0.25
+  recency_frames: 30    # candidate match must have been updated this recently
+
+# V4.2: track-context bridging (Phase 13) -- BoT-SORT reassigning a new
+# track_id to the same physically-unmoving downed person otherwise resets
+# all accumulated Mandown state to zero (measured: 74 tracked "persons" in
+# one real validation video under current settings). A brand-new track_id
+# whose first bbox closely overlaps a just-lost track's last position
+# adopts that track's existing context (history + state machine) instead of
+# starting fresh, then the existing gap-tolerance logic (TrackStateMachine.
+# on_gap) applies exactly as it already does for a same-ID detection gap.
+track_bridge:
+  iou_threshold: 0.3
+  # V4.3: raised from 30 -- a real observed gap on this session's RTSP
+  # camera (10fps) between a track's last confirmed-MANDOWN frame and its
+  # same-physical-person reappearance under a new id measured 107 frames
+  # (~10.7s), well beyond the old 30-frame/3s window. 300 frames (30s at
+  # 10fps) gives comfortable margin; iou_threshold, not this window, is
+  # the primary safety constraint against bridging to an unrelated person.
+  recency_frames: 300
+
+# V4.4: per-track, self-relative "has the hip dropped toward the floor
+# since this track was last confidently upright" signal -- replaces a V4.3
+# attempt that used FloorRegion (a scene-wide floor band built from many
+# people's ankle positions) evaluated at the hip. That proved too
+# imprecise for real camera perspective and caused two separate real-video
+# regressions (blocked genuine falls on top of the bends it was meant to
+# exclude) in one session. This needs no scene calibration at all, and is
+# never computed for a track with no prior standing observation --
+# including every "already lying at start" case, by design.
+hip_drop:
+  drop_threshold: 0.08
+  steepness: 15.0
+  upright_torso_angle_threshold: 0.15
+  # torso_angle alone is not enough: a person fallen toward/away from the
+  # camera ALSO reads torso_angle near 0 (that's exactly why angle-based
+  # cues are blind to that orientation) -- also requiring body_height_norm
+  # to look genuinely standing-height stops a foreshortened fall's own
+  # posture from being wrongly recorded as its "standing" baseline (found
+  # via real-video regression testing).
+  upright_body_height_norm_threshold: 0.85
+
+# V4.8: monocular 2D->3D pose lifting (src/pose_3d.py) -- the root-cause
+# fix for the foreshortening blind spot (a body pointed toward/away from
+# the camera has almost no lateral spread for ANY 2D-only angle feature
+# to measure). enabled=False (or mediapipe/the model file simply being
+# unavailable) makes every 3D-derived feature read as "no evidence"
+# everywhere it's consumed -- never a hard dependency.
+pose_3d:
+  enabled: true
+  model_path: "models/mediapipe/pose_landmarker_lite.task"
+  min_pose_detection_confidence: 0.3
+  min_visibility: 0.5   # below this mean landmark visibility, treat as no reading at all
+  crop_pad_ratio: 0.25  # BlazePose expects a full body with margin, not a tight box
+  # Real-time cost gate: only run 3D lifting when the cheap 2D height
+  # signal already looks suspicious (below this) or isn't calibrated yet
+  # at all -- never unconditionally on every normal standing frame. See
+  # src/config.py::Pose3DConfig for the full rationale.
+  height_gate_threshold: 0.85
+  # V6 Fix Set A (§2.2): per-side (asymmetric) torso-orientation
+  # correction. When one side's shoulder+hip landmarks are confidently
+  # more visible than the other's by more than this margin, that side's
+  # OWN shoulder->hip angle is also computed and the LARGER of it vs. the
+  # bilateral (midpoint) reading is kept -- provably monotonic (can only
+  # raise torso_angle_3d, never lower it). DESIGN MARGIN: the V6 spec's
+  # own suggested starting point, not yet tuned against a large real
+  # visibility-asymmetry dataset. See src/config.py::Pose3DConfig and
+  # src/pose_3d.py::Pose3DEstimator.estimate.
+  torso3d_asymmetry_threshold: 0.3
+
+# V6 Fix Set B: collapse_then_stillness -- a purely TEMPORAL confirmation
+# path (hard 0/1 gate) for a foreshortened/asymmetric lying posture that
+# no single-frame geometric signal above fully resolves. Requires a real
+# height-collapse SPIKE within the lookback window, followed by continuous
+# STILLNESS for the full still window, plus a real calibrated height
+# collapse right now. theta_spike/theta_still MEASURED from this repo's 2
+# real single-fall videos -- see src/config.py::MotionSignatureConfig and
+# MANDOWN_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT_V6 for the raw numbers.
+motion_signature:
+  t_lookback_seconds: 5.0
+  t_still_seconds: 5.0
+  theta_spike: 0.12    # MEASURED: below the weaker of the 2 real fall onsets (0.137)
+  theta_still: 0.06    # MEASURED: above both real events' post-onset settled p95 (0.012, 0.053)
+  height_collapse_floor: 0.5   # reuses the same calibrated floor as fusion/height_collapse
+
+# V6 Fix Set C (§4.1): narrow-range rotation search, run ONLY when the
+# plain straight-crop re-acquisition (pose_failure section above) already
+# failed to find a previously-tracked person at all. Same frozen YOLO-pose
+# model, no retraining -- see src/detector.py::PersonDetector.
+# redetect_in_roi_with_rotation and src/config.py::RotationSearchConfig.
+rotation_search:
+  enabled: true
+  angle_step_degrees: 15.0
+  angle_decay_factor: 0.9
+
+# V6 Fix Set C (§4.2): confidence-decayed synthetic keypoint carry-forward
+# for a brief TRUE detection gap (straight-crop AND rotation search both
+# already failed this frame). Bounded to t_gap_max_seconds of real,
+# continuous non-detection -- see src/config.py::DetectionRecoveryConfig
+# and src/mandown_track_context.py::MandownTrackContext.
+# extrapolated_keypoints. Cannot be exercised on a single static image --
+# only validated conceptually/via unit test this round; real-footage
+# validation deferred to when live-feed testing resumes (see V6 report §5).
+detection_recovery:
+  enabled: true
+  t_gap_max_seconds: 3.0
+  confidence_decay_factor: 0.85
+
+# Evidence fusion (Phase 8): combine LSTM confidence with independent
+# feature-based confidence. Transparent weighted rule-based fusion.
+# V3: current down/floor-state (feature) evidence is the primary Mandown
+# criterion, LSTM is supporting — rebalanced from V2's LSTM-majority weights.
+fusion:
+  weight_lstm: 0.35
+  weight_feature: 0.45
+  weight_persistence: 0.20
+  # A single very strong signal can push to POSSIBLE_MANDOWN even if the
+  # weighted sum is moderate (avoid requiring strict AND between sources).
+  strong_signal_threshold: 0.85
+  possible_mandown_threshold: 0.45
+  confirmed_mandown_threshold: 0.65
+  pose_quality_floor: 0.3   # below this pose_quality, discount all evidence toward "uncertain"
+  # V3: strong + persistent geometric evidence alone reaches full MANDOWN,
+  # without needing LSTM corroboration (an already-lying person must not
+  # wait on the LSTM's 30-frame buffer, or a weak/wrong LSTM read).
+  geometric_confirm_threshold: 0.60
+  geometric_confirm_persistence_threshold: 0.65
+  # V4: mirror-image safeguard — a confident LSTM alone, sustained via the
+  # state machine's streak, must not confirm MANDOWN with zero geometric
+  # grounding. Real case: M_D_2.mp4 track 694 (down_score<=0.20 and
+  # persistence_score=0.0 for the whole event, lstm_mandown_prob~0.99 alone
+  # plateaued fusion at ~0.46 long enough to confirm). Calibrated against 4
+  # real confirmed true positives (down_score>=0.27 at their earliest
+  # up-tier frame) with margin to spare.
+  lstm_only_geometric_grounding_down_floor: 0.22
+  lstm_only_geometric_grounding_persistence_floor: 0.05
+  # V4.1: real RTSP false positive -- sustained deep bending / a small
+  # low-quality sitting detection, both with moderate (not lying-level)
+  # down_score, reached confirmed MANDOWN via a confidently-wrong LSTM.
+  # Calibrated against all 4 real videos: every genuine confirmed MANDOWN
+  # has down_score in [0.704, 0.933] and already independently qualifies
+  # via geometric_confirm_threshold below; worst-case synthetic standing
+  # bend tops out at down_score~0.55. Only caps the LSTM-assisted path.
+  confirmed_mandown_down_floor: 0.65
+  # V4.2: alternate path to the floor above, for a person fallen toward/
+  # away from the camera (foreshortened -- angle-based cues stay near
+  # "upright", capping down_score below the floor above even after
+  # height-collapse corroboration). Three conditions, each excluding a
+  # DIFFERENT adversarial case -- floor_proximity_score alone is NOT
+  # enough: it also absorbs torso-angle evidence via max(), so a deep
+  # forward bend drives it just as high (0.89) as a genuine fall (0.74) --
+  # an earlier version of this gate used floor_proximity_score alone and
+  # reopened the V4.1 bending false positive through this new path.
+  # height_collapse_cue (driven only by body_height_norm, never by torso
+  # angle) is what actually excludes bending (~0.15 vs a genuine fall's
+  # ~0.93); pose_quality_floor excludes a separate adversarial case, an
+  # occluded seated person (~0.17 vs a genuine fall's ~0.48). See
+  # src/config.py::FusionConfig for the full measured breakdown.
+  confirmed_mandown_floor_proximity_floor: 0.70
+  confirmed_mandown_height_collapse_floor: 0.5
+  # V4.5: real RTSP false positive -- a person bending forward on their feet
+  # to reach the ground was confirmed MANDOWN through this path. This path
+  # exists because torso_angle is blind (~0.0) for a genuine foreshortened
+  # fall, but it never actually checked torso_angle was near-zero, so it
+  # fired just as easily for a deep bend (torso_angle~0.64, not blind at
+  # all -- down_score/kneeling_penalty already carry real "not down"
+  # evidence for that case, bypassed entirely by this path). See
+  # src/config.py::FusionConfig for the measured numbers.
+  alternate_grounding_torso_angle_ceiling: 0.2
+  # V4.7 (attempted, REVERTED): a fourth path combining moderate-but-
+  # elevated down_score/floor_proximity/height_collapse readings was tried
+  # for a real RTSP miss (person lying flat, torso_angle=0.22), but a
+  # synthetic crouching fixture measured comparable-or-higher numbers on
+  # the same three signals and reached MANDOWN under a confident LSTM once
+  # this path was added -- reverted before shipping. See
+  # src/config.py::FusionConfig for the measured numbers.
+  #
+  # V4.8: the genuinely new discriminator the V4.7 attempt needed, via
+  # monocular 2D->3D pose lifting (src/pose_3d.py) -- torso_angle_3d is a
+  # direct measurement of real torso orientation, so crouching (torso
+  # vertical in 3D despite a shortened bbox) reads LOW here, unlike the 2D
+  # height_collapse proxy that couldn't tell the two apart. Confident 3D
+  # lying evidence plus the same minimal geometric floor the LSTM-alone
+  # safeguard already requires is sufficient on its own -- not gated
+  # behind floor_proximity/height_collapse.
+  pose3d_lying_angle_floor: 0.55
+  # V6.1 (Objective 1): floor for body_axis_angle_3d (long-baseline
+  # shoulder->ankle 3D angle on the leg already confirmed via 2D keypoint
+  # confidence to be flat/extended -- never touches the hip landmark
+  # MediaPipe's kinematic prior was found to bias for a raised-knee
+  # configuration). Independent corroborator alongside torso_angle_3d,
+  # same gating. Defaults to the same value as pose3d_lying_angle_floor --
+  # not yet independently tuned against real footage. See
+  # src/config.py::FusionConfig for the full rationale.
+  pose3d_axis_lying_angle_floor: 0.55
+
+# Temporal state machine (Phase 9): hysteresis in frames to avoid single-frame
+# flicker triggering/clearing an alert.
+state_machine:
+  frames_to_confirm_mandown: 8      # consecutive strong-fusion frames before NORMAL/POSSIBLE -> MANDOWN
+  frames_to_enter_possible: 3       # consecutive moderate-fusion frames before NORMAL -> POSSIBLE_MANDOWN
+  frames_to_recover_normal: 45      # consecutive clearly-normal frames before MANDOWN/POSSIBLE -> NORMAL
+  cooldown_frames: 90               # min frames between repeated alert events for the same track
+
+# V2: pose-failure handling (Phase 3). When a track drops out of the normal
+# detection pass, retry a targeted ROI re-acquisition around its last known
+# location for up to hold_frames before giving up, and discount confidence
+# proportionally to how long the gap was.
+pose_failure:
+  hold_frames: 15
+  gap_tolerance_frames: 2            # gaps this short or shorter don't decay hysteresis progress
+  roi_reacquisition_padding_ratio: 0.6
+  max_reacquisitions_per_frame: 5    # bounds worst-case extra pose-model calls in one frame
+  min_confidence_multiplier: 0.5     # floor for the gap-length confidence discount
+  # V4.4: how long (wall-clock seconds) a confirmed-fallen track's last
+  # known box keeps drawing after it drops out of detection entirely --
+  # was a hardcoded 10s tied to nothing; real feedback found it created a
+  # visibly "stuck" red box + MANDOWN banner long after the person may
+  # have already gotten up and left, reading as a false alert with nobody
+  # there. Purely a rendering choice -- the underlying MANDOWN state is
+  # unaffected by how long this marker is drawn.
+  occluded_marker_seconds: 3.0
+
+logging_level: INFO

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Fall Detection CLI — process a video file or a live RTSP/webcam stream.
+
+Usage:
+    # Video file: drop it in input/, output goes to output/ automatically
+    python detect_falls.py --input video.mp4
+
+    # Explicit paths still work
+    python detect_falls.py --input video.mp4 --output result.mp4 --json-log events.json
+
+    # Live RTSP camera: real-time preview window, no inference video is written,
+    # only a screenshot per confirmed fall event (saved to events/)
+    python detect_falls.py --input rtsp://user:pass@camera-ip/stream
+
+    # Local webcam (index 0)
+    python detect_falls.py --input 0
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import logging
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from src.pipeline import FallDetectionPipeline
+
+logging.basicConfig(
+    level=logging.INFO,
+    format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s: %(message)s",
+)
+
+INPUT_DIR = Path("input")
+OUTPUT_DIR = Path("output")
+
+STREAM_PREFIXES = ("rtsp://", "rtsps://", "http://", "https://")
+
+
+def _is_stream_source(source: str) -> bool:
+    """True if `source` is an RTSP/HTTP stream URL or a webcam index."""
+    return source.startswith(STREAM_PREFIXES) or source.isdigit()
+
+
+def _resolve_input_path(raw_input: str) -> Path:
+    """Resolve a video file argument, checking input/ if it's a bare filename."""
+    path = Path(raw_input)
+    if path.exists():
+        return path
+    candidate = INPUT_DIR / raw_input
+    if candidate.exists():
+        return candidate
+    raise FileNotFoundError(
+        f"Video file not found: '{raw_input}' (also checked '{candidate}')"
+    )
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Detect falls using skeleton tracking + LSTM, on a video file or live stream"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--input", "-i", required=True,
+        help="Input video file (checked in input/ if not found as given), "
+        "an RTSP/HTTP stream URL, or a webcam index (e.g. 0)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output", "-o", default=None,
+        help="Output annotated video path (video files only; defaults to output/<name>.mp4)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--json-log", "-j", default=None,
+        help="JSON event log output path (defaults to output/<name>_events.json for video files)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--events-dir", default="events",
+        help="Folder where fall event screenshots are saved",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--no-display", action="store_true",
+        help="For live streams: don't open a preview window (still saves event screenshots)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--model", default="models/checkpoints/best.pth", help="LSTM model checkpoint"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--yolo-model", default="yolo11s-pose.pt", help="YOLO pose model")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--imgsz", type=int, default=1280, help="YOLO inference resolution (long side, in pixels)"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--confidence", type=float, default=0.40, help="Fall confidence threshold")
+    parser.add_argument("--cooldown", type=int, default=90, help="Cooldown frames between alerts")
+    parser.add_argument("--device", default=None, help="Device: cuda, cpu, or auto")
+
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    pipeline = FallDetectionPipeline(
+        yolo_model=args.yolo_model,
+        lstm_checkpoint=args.model,
+        device=args.device,
+        confidence_threshold=args.confidence,
+        cooldown_frames=args.cooldown,
+        events_dir=args.events_dir,
+        imgsz=args.imgsz,
+    )
+
+    if _is_stream_source(args.input):
+        source = int(args.input) if args.input.isdigit() else args.input
+        OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # Unlike the video-file branch below, a stream has no natural
+        # filename to default from -- without this, --json-log left unset
+        # means NOTHING gets saved when the stream stops (whether cleanly
+        # or via Ctrl+C), so a long-running camera session's event history
+        # is unrecoverable after the fact.
+        camera_id = FallDetectionPipeline._derive_camera_id(source)
+        json_path = args.json_log or (OUTPUT_DIR / f"{camera_id}_events.json")
+        result = pipeline.run_stream(
+            source=source,
+            display=not args.no_display,
+            json_path=json_path,
+        )
+    else:
+        input_path = _resolve_input_path(args.input)
+        OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        output_path = args.output or (OUTPUT_DIR / f"{input_path.stem}.mp4")
+        json_path = args.json_log or (OUTPUT_DIR / f"{input_path.stem}_events.json")
+
+        result = pipeline.process_video(
+            input_path=input_path,
+            output_path=output_path,
+            json_path=json_path,
+        )
+
+    return 0 if not result["summary"]["interrupted"] else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

MANDOWN V6

+

Asymmetric-Posture Geometric Fix, Temporal Motion-Signature Confirmation & Detection-Recovery — Implementation, Real-Image Validation & Honest Findings
+Prepared: September 2026  |  Validated against: 7 real live-camera screenshots (no live feed available this round) + the 4 standing reference videos

+ +
+Contents +
    +

    2. +
  2. Problem Restated: Two Independent Failure Modes
    3. +
  3. Fix Set A — Per-Side (Asymmetric-Aware) Geometric Features
    4. +
  4. Fix Set B — Motion-Signature Confirmation Path
    5. +
  5. Fix Set C — Detection-Recovery for Missed Poses
    6. +
  6. Real-Image Validation Results (7 Screenshots)
    7. +

    8. +

    9. +

    10. +

    11. +
+
+ +

1. Executive Summary

+

This round targeted two problems left open by the V5 report: (1A) a foreshortened-lying person whose limbs are posed +asymmetrically (a raised knee, a raised arm, an arm tucked under the torso) still doesn't reliably confirm, because +every existing angle feature averages left/right keypoints into one midpoint — an implicit symmetry assumption that +breaks exactly for this posture; and (1B) the pose model itself sometimes produces no detection at all for a person +already on the floor, undercounting a visibly-present fallen person.

+

Three fix sets were implemented, all gated to be either provably monotonic with respect to every existing confirmed +case, or purely additive/fallback-only, so the single most protected real regression case in this project +(M_D_2.mp4) could not be made worse by construction. This report documents exactly what was built, what +real measurement showed, and — matching this project's established discipline of recording negative results, not just +successes — an important honest finding: the specific visibility-asymmetry mechanism Fix Set A targets does +not actually explain the real §7.1 gap once re-measured against the real MediaPipe output for that exact frame. +The fix is safe and kept (it cannot regress anything and may help other real cases), but it did not close the original +target case on its own. Fix Set B (a temporal, not geometric, confirmation path) is the more promising path for that +specific gap, but by its own nature can only be validated on real video with genuine motion — untestable on the static +images available this round.

+

A serious-looking regression was also investigated this round: a fresh run of M_D_2.mp4 today produced +0 confirmed falls instead of the previously-reported 1. After a careful investigation (§7), this was +traced to this video's own already-documented tracker-fragmentation behavior (75-80 track IDs for one physically +continuous person), not to anything in this round's code changes — but it means the literal "exact-match" re-verification +requested could not be produced this round, and this is reported transparently rather than papered over.

+ +

2. Problem Restated: Two Independent Failure Modes

+

2.1 (1A) Asymmetric foreshortened-lying postures

+

Every angle feature in the pre-V6 pipeline (torso_angle, hip_angle, the 3D-lifted +torso_angle_3d) is computed from the midpoint of the left/right shoulder or hip pair, or the +midpoint-derived 3D center MediaPipe infers. Averaging two limbs into one number is an implicit symmetry assumption. +Foreshortened lying is exactly the case where that assumption breaks: one limb reads unambiguously "lying," the other +reads "bent/raised," and the average sits in the ambiguous middle where nothing confirms — documented in the V5 report +as the open §7.1 case (a person lying on their back with one knee raised): torso_angle_3d=0.319 (below the +0.55 floor), down_score=0.454 (below the 0.65 floor), floor_proximity=0.552 (below the 0.70 +floor).

+

2.2 (1B) The pose model itself sometimes fails to produce a detection at all

+

YOLO-pose, like nearly every pose model, is trained overwhelmingly on upright/walking/sports imagery. Prone, +floor-level, foreshortened bodies are underrepresented in that distribution, so both detection confidence and keypoint +quality degrade on exactly the frames MANDOWN most needs to see clearly — a data-distribution problem in the frozen +model, worked around at inference time (not fixed by retuning fusion thresholds, and not by retraining).

+ +

3. Fix Set A — Per-Side (Asymmetric-Aware) Geometric Features

+ +

3.1 §2.1 — Per-leg leg_extension_ratio

+

Investigation found this selection rule was already implemented, independently, in an earlier +engineering round: ExtendedFeatureExtractor._leg_extension_ratio computes each leg's hip→knee→ankle +extension ratio separately and only includes a leg whose three keypoints are all confidently visible; when exactly one +leg qualifies, that leg's ratio is used alone (never blended with a low-confidence value); when neither qualifies, it +returns a neutral "no bend evidence" default rather than fabricating one. This is functionally identical to the V6 +spec's requested selection rule. New tests (TestLegExtensionRatioPerSideSelection, in +tests/test_extended_features.py) now assert this exact behavior explicitly, closing the gap between "this +happens to already work" and "this is verified to work."

+

No threshold value was changed here: the spec's suggested τ_vis=0.5 (vs. the existing 0.3) was deliberately +not adopted, since the spec's own guidance explicitly warns against tuning this in isolation from a +large real keypoint-confidence dataset, which this round did not have (no live feed).

+ +

3.2 §2.2 — Per-side torso_angle_3d, provably monotonic via max()

+

Implemented in src/pose_3d.py. When one side's shoulder+hip MediaPipe landmarks are confidently more +visible than the other's by more than Pose3DConfig.torso3d_asymmetry_threshold (0.3, a design margin — the +spec's own suggested starting point), that side's own shoulder→hip vector is computed as a second candidate +angle, and the larger of it vs. the existing bilateral (midpoint) reading is kept:

+
torso_angle_3d = max(bilateral_angle, single_side_angle)   # only when |w_L - w_R| > threshold
+                                                             # else: bilateral_angle, byte-identical to pre-V6
+
+Why this is provably monotonic: a symmetric-visibility body (the common case, including every existing +confirmed real fall in this repo) takes the unchanged bilateral-only path — zero behavior change. An asymmetric-visibility +body can only have its angle raised relative to the pre-V6 value, never lowered, since max() never +selects a smaller number over the one that was already there. This means the fix cannot regress any existing confirmed +case by mathematical construction, independent of any live-camera re-verification. +
+

Verified with 5 new unit tests (TestPose3DPerSideMonotonicMax, tests/test_pose_3d.py) using +a mocked MediaPipe result for precise control: symmetric visibility stays byte-identical to bilateral; an asymmetric +fixture modeled on the real §7.1 corruption mechanism (a raised knee pulling one hip toward the shoulder) shows the +single-side reading correctly wins via max(); a visibility gap below the threshold stays bilateral (no +over-triggering on ordinary noise); a genuinely upright person with incidental visibility asymmetry stays correctly low +(both readings are low, so max() changes nothing).

+ +

3.2.1 Real-image re-measurement — the honest finding

+

Re-running this exact fix against the real §7.1 frame (2026-09-14 18:19:32 screenshot) to see whether it actually +raises torso_angle_3d for the real target case produced a genuinely important, unglamorous result:

+
L_SHOULDER visibility=0.999   L_HIP visibility=0.998
+R_SHOULDER visibility=0.999   R_HIP visibility=0.997
+w_L = 0.997   w_R = 0.997   |w_L - w_R| = 0.0002   (threshold: 0.3 -- NOT crossed)
+=> per-side path never activates; result stays bilateral-only: torso_angle_3d = 0.236
+
+MediaPipe is confidently wrong here, not uncertain. The hypothesis behind Fix 2.2 was that a raised +knee drags visibility DOWN on the corrupted side, creating a detectable asymmetry. On this real frame (and on 2 other +real lying postures re-measured the same way — the "arm raised" and "symmetric lying" screenshots, see §6), MediaPipe +reports near-identical, high visibility on both sides even though its inferred 3D position is +apparently still off for this posture. The corruption here is a genuine 3D-pose-inference inaccuracy for an +underrepresented posture, not a visibility-detectable asymmetry — so the specific mechanism this fix targets does not +explain, and does not close, the original real gap it was written for. +
+

The fix is kept anyway: it is safe (provably monotonic, independently unit-tested), free (near-zero extra cost — the +extra angle computation is a few vector operations, not a second model inference), and may still help a different real +scenario where visibility genuinely does diverge (e.g., a limb entirely outside the frame or heavily occluded by +furniture, rather than merely differently posed). It is reported as "implemented and safe, did not close the target +case" rather than overclaimed — the same honesty standard the V4.7/V4.9 investigations in the V5 report were held to.

+ +

3.3 §2.1's hip_angle per-side replacement — deliberately NOT implemented this round

+

The spec also requested a per-side, asymmetric-aware hip_angle. This was evaluated and not +implemented, for a specific, provable safety reason rather than a time constraint: hip_angle +currently feeds a subtractive exclusion gate — the V4.9 hip_torso_mismatch signal +(mismatch = torso_angle - hip_angle) that protects against the real deep-bend false positive documented in +the V5 report. Raising hip_angle for an asymmetric case would shrink that mismatch, making the +bend-exclusion signature less likely to fire — i.e., a change that helps one real case could simultaneously +weaken the protection for a different, already-fixed real false positive. Unlike torso_angle_3d (where +"higher is always more like lying, so raising it is always the safe direction"), hip_angle sits on both +sides of this tension at once, so no single max()/min() trick makes it safe in both directions +simultaneously without a live-footage re-verification pass this round did not have access to. Deferred, and flagged as +the top open item in §9 — this mirrors the V5 report's own precedent of reverting/deferring a change the moment its +safety could not be proven, rather than shipping something merely "probably fine."

+ +

4. Fix Set B — Motion-Signature Confirmation Path

+ +

A purely temporal, not geometric, confirmation path: collapse_then_stillness, computed +per track in MandownTrackContext and consumed as a new, additive rule 8 in EvidenceFusion. A +hard 0/1 gate (never blended), True only when all of:

+
    +
  1. a genuine body_height_norm collapse of at least theta_spike within a 1-second window, + somewhere in the last t_lookback_seconds + t_still_seconds;
    2. +
  2. continuous stillness (per-frame keypoint motion energy below theta_still) held from that spike + through to now, for at least t_still_seconds;
    3. +
  3. a real, currently-elevated height_collapse_cue (reuses the same calibrated floor established in + V4.2-V4.9);
    4. +
  4. the track is not currently inside its own confidently-standing baseline.
    5. +
+
if collapse_then_stillness and pose_quality >= pose_quality_floor:
+    fusion_score = max(fusion_score, confirmed_mandown_threshold)   # same style as V4.10's direct down_score path
+

This is additive by construction — it can only ever raise the fusion score for a track already backed by a real, +sustained height collapse; it cannot fire for, and cannot suppress, anything else.

+ +

4.1 Thresholds measured from real footage, not guessed

+

Per the spec's own instruction, theta_spike/theta_still were measured from this repo's 2 +real single-fall videos via a dedicated diagnostic pass (not a live camera — these are pre-existing repo assets):

+ + + + +
Video / track1s collapse velocity at real fall onsetPost-onset "settled" motion-energy (p95)
mandown_2.mp4 track 10.5600.012
man_down_c08.mp4 track 10.1370.053
+

theta_spike=0.12 sits just below the weaker of the two real onsets; theta_still=0.06 sits +just above the higher of the two real "settled" readings (real footage is never perfectly motionless — ongoing minor +jitter/breathing/pose-estimation noise is normal, even while genuinely lying still). Explicitly labeled in-code and here +as a conservative first pass from a small (n=2) real sample, not a fully-tuned production threshold — +set with margin toward not falsely triggering, since every real confirmed case in this repo already confirms through an +existing path independent of this rule ever firing.

+ +

4.2 Unit-tested negative controls (per spec §3.4)

+ + + + + + + +
Negative controlWhich condition failsResult
Deliberate, gradual sit-down (height declines slowly over 10s, not sharply within 1s)(a) no genuine spikeCorrectly rejected
Chair scoot-back (height never really collapses)(c) height_collapse_cue stays lowCorrectly rejected
Bending to help someone, then standing back up (motion resumes 2s after the spike, well before the 5s stillness window completes)(b) stillness doesn't sustainCorrectly rejected
Track currently reading confidently upright(d)Correctly rejected
Freshly-created track, no historyinsufficient dataCorrectly rejected, no crash
+ +

4.3 What could and could not be validated without live video

+

Per the spec's own explicit acknowledgment, the TRUE-POSITIVE path is inherently temporal and cannot be exercised on +a static image. What was run: feeding one of the real still images repeatedly as a synthetic zero-motion, +zero-height-change 200-frame "sequence" —

+
PASS: collapse_then_stillness stayed False for 200 static-repeat frames (no genuine spike ever occurred)
+

This proves the gate does not false-trigger on a static/frozen feed, but is not a substitute for +validating the true-positive path on a real fall clip — that remains deferred to when live-feed testing resumes, exactly +as the spec anticipated.

+ +

5. Fix Set C — Detection-Recovery for Missed Poses

+ +

5.1 §4.1 — Narrow-range rotation search

+

+"""LSTM-based fall detection classifier."""
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+
+
+class FallDetector(nn.Module):
+    """LSTM classifier for fall detection from skeleton feature sequences.
+
+    Input: (batch, seq_len, input_size) — temporal sequences of skeleton features.
+    Output: (batch, num_classes) — class logits for normal/falling/fallen.
+    """
+
+    CLASS_NAMES = {0: "normal", 1: "falling", 2: "fallen"}
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        input_size: int = 5,
+        hidden_size: int = 128,
+        num_layers: int = 2,
+        num_classes: int = 3,
+        dropout: float = 0.3,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.input_size = input_size
+        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
+        self.num_layers = num_layers
+        self.num_classes = num_classes
+
+        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
+            input_size=input_size,
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            num_layers=num_layers,
+            batch_first=True,
+            dropout=dropout if num_layers > 1 else 0.0,
+        )
+        self.layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
+        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_classes)
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Forward pass.
+
+        Args:
+            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, seq_len, input_size).
+
+        Returns:
+            Logits of shape (batch, num_classes).
+        """
+        # LSTM output: (batch, seq_len, hidden_size)
+        lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(x)
+        # Use last timestep output
+        last_hidden = lstm_out[:, -1, :]
+        out = self.layer_norm(last_hidden)
+        out = self.dropout(out)
+        return self.fc(out)
+
+    def predict(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Predict class and confidence.
+
+        Args:
+            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, seq_len, input_size).
+
+        Returns:
+            Tuple of (predicted_classes, confidences).
+        """
+        self.eval()
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            logits = self.forward(x)
+            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
+            confidences, predictions = torch.max(probs, dim=1)
+        return predictions, confidences

+"""Batch test fall detection on all test videos and generate a summary report.
+
+Usage:

+"""
+
+import argparse

+

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+VIDEO_EXTENSIONS = {".mp4", ".avi", ".mov", ".mkv"}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Batch test fall detection")
+    parser.add_argument("--input", "-i", default="tests/test_videos/",
+                        help="Directory with test videos")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", "-o", default="output/test_results/",
+                        help="Output directory for results")
+    parser.add_argument("--confidence", type=float, default=0.7)
+    parser.add_argument("--device", default=None)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    input_dir = Path(args.input)
+    output_dir = Path(args.output)
+    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    # Find all test videos
+    videos = sorted(
+        f for f in input_dir.iterdir()
+        if f.suffix.lower() in VIDEO_EXTENSIONS
+    )
+
+    if not videos:
+        logger.error(f"No video files found in {input_dir}")
+        return
+
+    logger.info(f"Found {len(videos)} test videos in {input_dir}")
+    logger.info("=" * 70)
+
+    # Initialize pipeline once
+    pipeline = FallDetectionPipeline(
+        confidence_threshold=args.confidence,
+        device=args.device,
+    )
+
+    # Process each video
+    all_results = []
+    total_start = time.time()
+
+    for i, video_path in enumerate(videos, 1):
+        name = video_path.stem
+        logger.info(f"\n[{i}/{len(videos)}] Processing: {video_path.name}")
+
+        out_video = output_dir / f"{name}_result.mp4"
+        out_json = output_dir / f"{name}_events.json"
+
+        try:
+            result = pipeline.process_video(
+                input_path=video_path,
+                output_path=out_video,
+                json_path=out_json,
+            )
+            result["video_name"] = video_path.name
+            result["status"] = "success"
+            all_results.append(result)
+
+        except Exception as e:
+            logger.error(f"Failed to process {video_path.name}: {e}")
+            all_results.append({
+                "video_name": video_path.name,
+                "status": "error",
+                "error": str(e),
+            })
+
+    total_time = time.time() - total_start
+
+    # Generate summary report
+    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
+    logger.info("BATCH TEST SUMMARY")
+    logger.info("=" * 70)
+
+    summary = {
+        "total_videos": len(videos),
+        "successful": sum(1 for r in all_results if r["status"] == "success"),
+        "failed": sum(1 for r in all_results if r["status"] == "error"),
+        "total_processing_time": round(total_time, 1),
+        "confidence_threshold": args.confidence,
+        "results": [],
+    }
+
+    for r in all_results:
+        if r["status"] == "success":
+            entry = {
+                "video": r["video_name"],
+                "falls_detected": r["summary"]["total_falls"],
+                "persons_tracked": r["summary"]["persons_tracked"],
+                "processing_time": r["summary"]["processing_time_seconds"],
+                "events": r["events"],
+            }
+            summary["results"].append(entry)
+
+            falls = r["summary"]["total_falls"]
+            persons = r["summary"]["persons_tracked"]
+            ptime = r["summary"]["processing_time_seconds"]
+            logger.info(
+                f"  {r['video_name']:<35} | "
+                f"Falls: {falls} | Persons: {persons} | Time: {ptime:.1f}s"
+            )
+        else:
+            summary["results"].append({
+                "video": r["video_name"],
+                "status": "error",
+                "error": r.get("error", "unknown"),
+            })
+            logger.info(f"  {r['video_name']:<35} | ERROR: {r.get('error', 'unknown')}")
+
+    total_falls = sum(
+        r.get("summary", {}).get("total_falls", 0)
+        for r in all_results if r["status"] == "success"
+    )
+    logger.info(f"\nTotal falls detected across all videos: {total_falls}")
+    logger.info(f"Total processing time: {total_time:.1f}s")
+
+    # Save summary
+    summary_path = output_dir / "batch_summary.json"
+    with open(summary_path, "w") as f:
+        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)
+    logger.info(f"Summary saved to {summary_path}")
+    logger.info(f"All results in {output_dir}/")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Benchmark candidate person detectors for the ROI-pose pipeline.
+
+Compares the current full-frame YOLO11-Pose baseline against dedicated
+bbox-only person detectors (yolo11n / yolov8n / yolo11s) on person recall
+and speed, over a chosen frame range of a video. Prioritizes recall over
+precision — a missed person means pose inference cannot happen at all.
+
+Reports both "any-person recall" (at least one person detected anywhere in
+frame) and, if `--target-region` is given, recall specifically for that
+region (IoU > 0.1 with a detected box) — the metric that actually matters
+when checking whether a detector can find a *specific* hard-to-see person
+(e.g. someone lying down) rather than any bystander in the scene.
+
+Usage:
+    python scripts/benchmark_person_detector.py --video input/man_down_zoomed_demo__2_.mp4 \
+        --start 490 --end 560 --target-region 590,405,960,590
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import cv2
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
+
+from src.detector import LightweightPersonDetector, PersonDetector  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def _iou(box_a, box_b):
+    ax1, ay1, ax2, ay2 = box_a
+    bx1, by1, bx2, by2 = box_b
+    ix1, iy1 = max(ax1, bx1), max(ay1, by1)
+    ix2, iy2 = min(ax2, bx2), min(ay2, by2)
+    inter = max(0.0, ix2 - ix1) * max(0.0, iy2 - iy1)
+    area_a = max(0.0, ax2 - ax1) * max(0.0, ay2 - ay1)
+    area_b = max(0.0, bx2 - bx1) * max(0.0, by2 - by1)
+    union = area_a + area_b - inter
+    return inter / union if union > 0 else 0.0
+
+
+def _run(name: str, boxes_per_frame, elapsed: float, total_frames: int, target_region) -> dict:
+    frames_any = sum(1 for boxes in boxes_per_frame if len(boxes) > 0)
+    frames_target = None
+    if target_region is not None:
+        frames_target = sum(
+            1 for boxes in boxes_per_frame if any(_iou(b, target_region) > 0.1 for b in boxes)
+        )
+    target_recall = None
+    if frames_target is not None:
+        target_recall = frames_target / max(total_frames, 1)
+    return {
+        "name": name,
+        "total_frames": total_frames,
+        "any_recall": frames_any / max(total_frames, 1),
+        "target_recall": target_recall,
+        "fps": total_frames / max(elapsed, 1e-6),
+    }
+
+
+def benchmark_full_frame_pose(video_path, start, end, target_region) -> dict:
+    detector = PersonDetector(model_name="yolo11n-pose.pt", confidence_threshold=0.05)
+    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
+    boxes_per_frame, total = [], 0
+    t0 = time.time()
+    for frame_num in range(end):
+        ret, frame = cap.read()
+        if not ret:
+            break
+        if frame_num < start:
+            continue
+        result = detector.detect_frame(frame, frame_num)
+        boxes_per_frame.append([p.bbox for p in result.persons])
+        total += 1
+    elapsed = time.time() - t0
+    cap.release()
+    name = "yolo11n-pose.pt (full-frame, current baseline)"
+    return _run(name, boxes_per_frame, elapsed, total, target_region)
+
+
+def benchmark_bbox_detector(model_name: str, video_path, start, end, target_region) -> dict:
+    detector = LightweightPersonDetector(model_name=model_name, confidence_threshold=0.05)
+    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
+    boxes_per_frame, total = [], 0
+    t0 = time.time()
+    for frame_num in range(end):
+        ret, frame = cap.read()
+        if not ret:
+            break
+        if frame_num < start:
+            continue
+        tracked = detector.track_frame(frame)
+        boxes_per_frame.append([t.bbox for t in tracked])
+        total += 1
+    elapsed = time.time() - t0
+    cap.release()
+    return _run(model_name, boxes_per_frame, elapsed, total, target_region)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Benchmark person-detector candidates")
+    parser.add_argument("--video", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--start", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--end", type=int, default=200)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--target-region", default=None,
+        help="x1,y1,x2,y2 of a specific person to check recall for (e.g. a hard-to-detect person)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--candidates", nargs="+", default=["yolo11n.pt", "yolov8n.pt"],
+        help="bbox-only detector model names to benchmark against the full-frame pose baseline",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    target_region = None
+    if args.target_region:
+        target_region = tuple(float(v) for v in args.target_region.split(","))
+
+    results = [benchmark_full_frame_pose(args.video, args.start, args.end, target_region)]
+    for name in args.candidates:
+        results.append(
+            benchmark_bbox_detector(name, args.video, args.start, args.end, target_region)
+        )
+
+    header = f"{'Model':45s} {'AnyRecall':>10s} {'TargetRecall':>13s} {'FPS':>8s}"
+    print(f"\n{header}")
+    print("-" * len(header))
+    for r in results:
+        target_str = f"{r['target_recall']:.1%}" if r["target_recall"] is not None else "n/a"
+        print(f"{r['name']:45s} {r['any_recall']:>9.1%} {target_str:>13s} {r['fps']:>7.1f}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""V4 Step 5/9: synthetic camera-angle validation matrix.
+
+Honest scope: from 2D COCO keypoints alone (no 3D body model), the only
+camera-condition dimensions that can be genuinely simulated -- not
+fabricated -- are (a) in-image-plane camera ROLL/TILT (rotate the whole
+skeleton around a center point) and (b) DISTANCE (scale the skeleton/bbox
+toward the frame center). Camera ELEVATION (low/medium/high) and
+ORIENTATION (front/rear/side/diagonal relative to the subject) change how
+a 3D pose projects into 2D in ways a flat rotation/scale of an already-2D
+skeleton cannot faithfully reproduce -- simulating those would fabricate
+data, not validate anything, so they are NOT covered here. Real footage
+(4 videos) already covers 3 distinct real camera setups per
+MANDOWN_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md; this script covers roll x distance x
+person-orientation, which real footage does not systematically vary.
+
+Reports whether each combination reaches MANDOWN, POSSIBLE_MANDOWN, or
+stays NORMAL. SYNTHETIC ONLY. Throwaway reporting tool.
+"""
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
+
+import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
+
+from tests.test_already_lying_integration import (  # noqa: E402
+    FRAME_H,
+    FRAME_W,
+    _StaticTrackSimulator,
+    _bbox_for,
+    diagonal_lying_keypoints,
+    prone_lying_keypoints,
+    side_lying_keypoints,
+    standing_keypoints,
+    supine_lying_keypoints,
+)
+
+PERSON_ORIENTATIONS = [
+    ("supine", supine_lying_keypoints),
+    ("prone", prone_lying_keypoints),
+    ("side (bent knees)", side_lying_keypoints),
+    ("diagonal", diagonal_lying_keypoints),
+    ("standing (negative control)", standing_keypoints),
+]
+
+ROLLS_DEG = [0, 15, 30, 45]
+DISTANCES = [("near", 1.4), ("medium", 1.0), ("far", 0.6)]
+
+
+def transform(kps: np.ndarray, roll_deg: float, scale: float) -> np.ndarray:
+    import math
+
+    cx, cy = FRAME_W / 2, FRAME_H / 2
+    rad = math.radians(roll_deg)
+    cos_a, sin_a = math.cos(rad), math.sin(rad)
+    out = kps.copy()
+    for i in range(kps.shape[0]):
+        x, y, conf = kps[i]
+        dx, dy = (x - cx) * scale, (y - cy) * scale
+        out[i] = [cx + dx * cos_a - dy * sin_a, cy + dx * sin_a + dy * cos_a, conf]
+    return out
+
+
+def run(kps: np.ndarray) -> tuple[str, float]:
+    sim = _StaticTrackSimulator()
+    bbox = _bbox_for(kps)
+    state = None
+    for frame_num in range(40):
+        state = sim.step(kps, bbox)
+        if state.name == "MANDOWN":

+    scores = sim.scorer.score(sim.base_history[-1], ext, sim.base_history, sim.ext_history)
+    return state.name, scores.mandown_confidence
+
+
+header = f"{'orientation':<30} {'roll':>5} {'distance':>9}  {'result':<10} conf"
+print(header)
+print("-" * len(header))
+algorithm_failures = []
+for name, fn in PERSON_ORIENTATIONS:
+    base_kps = fn()
+    for roll in ROLLS_DEG:

+            result, conf = run(kps)
+            print(f"{name:<30} {roll:>4}° {dist_name:>9}  {result:<10} {conf:.3f}")
+            is_lying = name != "standing (negative control)"
+            if is_lying and result == "NORMAL":
+                algorithm_failures.append((name, roll, dist_name, conf))
+            if not is_lying and result != "NORMAL":
+                algorithm_failures.append((name, roll, dist_name, conf))
+
+print()
+print(f"Non-NORMAL-as-expected cases: {len(algorithm_failures)}")
+for f in algorithm_failures:
+    print(f"  {f}")

+"""Per-frame diagnostic dump for one tracked person, for MANDOWN investigation.
+
+Monkey-patches (does not modify) the real pipeline components to capture
+every signal that feeds a MANDOWN decision for a specific track_id over a
+frame range: raw keypoints, base+extended feature values, feature-scorer
+outputs, fusion inputs/outputs, and final state.
+
+Not part of the production pipeline or the permanent test suite -- a
+throwaway investigation tool, reusable across videos/tracks.
+
+Usage:
+    python scripts/debug_track_diagnostics.py <video> <track_id> \
+        [--frame-start N] [--frame-end N] [--out path.json]
+"""
+

+import json
+import sys
+from dataclasses import asdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

+

+    parser.add_argument("video")
+    parser.add_argument("track_id", type=int, help="-1 to capture ALL tracks in the frame range")
+    parser.add_argument("--frame-start", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--frame-end", type=int, default=10**9)
+    parser.add_argument("--out", default=None)

+                         help="Additional track_ids to also capture (for fragmentation investigation)")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    targets = {args.track_id, *args.other_track_ids}
+    capture_all = args.track_id == -1
+
+    pipeline = FallDetectionPipeline()
+
+    state = {"frame_num": -1, "tid": None}
+    records: list[dict] = []
+
+    orig_detect_frame = pipeline.detector.detect_frame
+
+    def wrapped_detect_frame(frame, frame_num):
+        state["frame_num"] = frame_num
+        return orig_detect_frame(frame, frame_num)
+
+    pipeline.detector.detect_frame = wrapped_detect_frame
+
+    orig_get_or_create = pipeline.mandown_contexts.get_or_create
+
+    def wrapped_get_or_create(tid):
+        state["tid"] = tid
+        return orig_get_or_create(tid)
+
+    pipeline.mandown_contexts.get_or_create = wrapped_get_or_create
+
+    def in_scope() -> bool:
+        if not (args.frame_start <= state["frame_num"] <= args.frame_end):

+        return capture_all or state["tid"] in targets
+
+    orig_ext_extract = pipeline.ext_feature_extractor.extract
+

+        ext = orig_ext_extract(keypoints, bbox, frame_width, frame_height, **kwargs)

+            records.append({
+                "frame_num": state["frame_num"],
+                "track_id": state["tid"],
+                "keypoints": keypoints.tolist(),
+                "bbox": list(bbox),
+                "frame_width": frame_width,
+                "frame_height": frame_height,
+                "ext": asdict(ext),
+            })
+        return ext
+
+    pipeline.ext_feature_extractor.extract = wrapped_ext_extract
+
+    orig_score = pipeline.feature_scorer.score
+
+    def wrapped_score(base, ext, base_history, ext_history, floor_contact_score=0.0):
+        result = orig_score(base, ext, base_history, ext_history,
+                             floor_contact_score=floor_contact_score)
+        if records and in_scope() and records[-1]["frame_num"] == state["frame_num"]:
+            records[-1]["base"] = asdict(base)
+            records[-1]["floor_contact_score_input"] = floor_contact_score
+            records[-1]["feature_scores"] = result.to_dict()
+        return result
+
+    pipeline.feature_scorer.score = wrapped_score
+
+    orig_combine = pipeline.fusion.combine
+
+    def wrapped_combine(**kwargs):
+        result = orig_combine(**kwargs)
+        if records and in_scope() and records[-1]["frame_num"] == state["frame_num"]:
+            records[-1]["fusion_inputs"] = kwargs
+            records[-1]["fusion_result"] = result.to_dict()
+        return result
+
+    pipeline.fusion.combine = wrapped_combine
+
+    out_path = Path(args.out) if args.out else Path(f"/tmp/track_{args.track_id}_diagnostics.json")
+    print(f"Processing {args.video} for track {sorted(targets)}, frames "
