+"""Camera-independent scene normalization.
+
+Does NOT attempt to measure physical camera height. Instead builds a
+per-camera profile from runtime observations: how expected person bbox
+size varies with full 2D image position (row AND column -- a
+ground-plane-referenced perspective-scale regression, not a row-only
+one), so the same real-world posture produces comparable normalized
+features regardless of camera tilt/height/zoom/column.
+
+If too few reliable samples have been observed, parameters are marked
+unavailable/low-confidence rather than invented — callers should fall
+back to plain frame-relative normalization in that case.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import threading
+from collections import deque
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from src.config import CalibrationConfig, FloorRegionConfig
+from src.person_size_stats import RollingPersonSizeStats, SizeStatsSnapshot
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FloorRegion:
+    """Estimated image-row band where this camera's tracked people actually
+    touch the ground, from observed ankle y-positions — not assumed to be
+    the bottom of the frame. Not a 3D reconstruction: purely an empirical
+    band in image space, with an explicit confidence."""
+
+    band_low: float = 0.0
+    band_high: float = 0.0
+    confidence: float = 0.0
+    num_samples: int = 0
+
+    @property
+    def is_valid(self) -> bool:
+        return self.confidence > 0.0 and self.band_high > self.band_low
+
+    def contact_likelihood(self, y: float) -> float:
+        """1.0 when y falls inside the floor band, decaying smoothly outside
+        it (normalized by the band's own half-width). 0.0 (no evidence)
+        when the band isn't calibrated — never a fabricated value."""
+        if not self.is_valid:
+            return 0.0
+        half_width = max((self.band_high - self.band_low) / 2.0, 1e-3)
+        center = (self.band_high + self.band_low) / 2.0
+        distance = max(0.0, abs(y - center) - half_width)
+        return float(np.exp(-distance / half_width)) * self.confidence
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScenePerspectiveFit:
+    """Ground-plane-referenced fit of expected bbox height/width as a
+    function of full 2D image position (row AND column), not row alone.
+
+    height_at(x, y) ~= coef_h_x*x + coef_h_y*y + intercept_h, fit over
+    (ankle_x, bbox_bottom_y, bbox_height) triples from reliable
+    standing-like detections. A camera looking down at an angle (any real
+    mounted CCTV camera) has perspective scale that varies across BOTH
+    axes, not just vertically -- a person near a side edge of the frame at
+    the same row as someone near the center is not the same real distance
+    from the camera in general (this is most visible on a wide/fisheye-ish
+    lens, where the earlier row-only fit's "expected size" was only
+    correct along one column and increasingly wrong toward the frame
+    edges). Still an empirical, auto-calibrating regression from
+    accumulated observations -- not a true metric ground-plane homography
+    (that needs known real-world reference distances this system never
+    has), but the 2D-position dependence is the specific gap a 1D,
+    row-only fit had."""
+
+    coef_h_x: float = 0.0
+    coef_h_y: float = 0.0
+    intercept_h: float = 0.0
+    coef_w_x: float = 0.0
+    coef_w_y: float = 0.0
+    intercept_w: float = 0.0
+    r_squared: float = 0.0
+    num_samples: int = 0
+
+    def height_at(self, x: float, y: float) -> float:
+        return self.coef_h_x * x + self.coef_h_y * y + self.intercept_h
+
+    @property
+    def is_valid(self) -> bool:
+        return self.num_samples >= 15 and self.r_squared > 0.1
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SceneProfile:
+    """Per-camera scene/normalization profile, built and refined at runtime."""
+
+    camera_id: str
+    frame_width: int
+    frame_height: int
+    calibration_confidence: float = 0.0
+    perspective: ScenePerspectiveFit = field(default_factory=ScenePerspectiveFit)
+    size_stats: SizeStatsSnapshot | None = None
+    # "flat" | "tilted_up_left" | "tilted_up_right" | "unknown"
+    dominant_floor_direction: str = "unknown"
+    floor_region: FloorRegion = field(default_factory=FloorRegion)
+
+    def normalize_height(
+        self, bbox_bottom_y: float, observed_height: float, bbox_center_x: float
+    ) -> float:
+        """Return observed_height / expected_standing_height, i.e. a
+        camera-position-independent ratio (~1.0 = normal standing size,
+        <1.0 = shorter than expected — e.g. lying reduces vertical extent).
+
+        Prefers the position-aware perspective regression (accounts for
+        near/far perspective scaling across BOTH image axes, not just
+        row); falls back to the position-agnostic rolling median when the
+        regression isn't calibrated yet; falls back to a neutral 1.0 (no
+        signal) when nothing is calibrated at all — never a fabricated
+        value. `bbox_center_x` is required (not optional/defaulted) since
+        the fit now genuinely depends on it — a caller that doesn't track
+        horizontal position has no correct value to substitute.
+        """
+        if self.perspective.is_valid:
+            expected = self.perspective.height_at(bbox_center_x, bbox_bottom_y)
+            if expected > 1e-3:
+                return observed_height / expected
+
+        if self.size_stats is not None and self.size_stats.is_calibrated:
+            expected = self.size_stats.median_height
+            if expected and expected > 1e-3:
+                return observed_height / expected
+
+        return 1.0
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
+        return {
+            "camera_id": self.camera_id,
+            "frame_width": self.frame_width,
+            "frame_height": self.frame_height,
+            "calibration_confidence": round(self.calibration_confidence, 3),
+            "dominant_floor_direction": self.dominant_floor_direction,
+            "perspective": {
+                "coef_h_x": self.perspective.coef_h_x,
+                "coef_h_y": self.perspective.coef_h_y,
+                "intercept_h": self.perspective.intercept_h,
+                "coef_w_x": self.perspective.coef_w_x,
+                "coef_w_y": self.perspective.coef_w_y,
+                "intercept_w": self.perspective.intercept_w,
+                "r_squared": self.perspective.r_squared,
+                "num_samples": self.perspective.num_samples,
+                "is_valid": self.perspective.is_valid,
+            },
+            "floor_region": {
+                "band_low": self.floor_region.band_low,
+                "band_high": self.floor_region.band_high,
+                "confidence": round(self.floor_region.confidence, 3),
+                "num_samples": self.floor_region.num_samples,
+                "is_valid": self.floor_region.is_valid,
+            },
+            "size_stats": (
+                {
+                    "sample_count": self.size_stats.sample_count,
+                    "median_height": self.size_stats.median_height,
+                    "p25_height": self.size_stats.p25_height,
+                    "p75_height": self.size_stats.p75_height,
+                    "height_std": self.size_stats.height_std,
+                    "median_width": self.size_stats.median_width,
+                    "p25_width": self.size_stats.p25_width,
+                    "p75_width": self.size_stats.p75_width,
+                    "calibration_confidence": round(self.size_stats.calibration_confidence, 3),
+                    "is_calibrated": self.size_stats.is_calibrated,
+                }
+                if self.size_stats is not None
+                else None
+            ),
+        }
+
+
+class SceneProfileBuilder:
+    """Accumulates (bbox_bottom_y, height, width, ankle_x) samples for one
+    camera and periodically refits the perspective regression. Thread-safe
+    and cheap enough to update every frame; the expensive refit only runs
+    every `refit_stride` new samples, not on every observation."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        camera_id: str,
+        frame_width: int,
+        frame_height: int,
+        cal: CalibrationConfig | None = None,
+        floor_region_config: FloorRegionConfig | None = None,
+        refit_stride: int = 10,
+        max_samples: int = 500,
+        sample_log_dir: str | Path | None = None,
+        sample_log_max_rows: int = 50,
+    ):
+        self.camera_id = camera_id
+        self.frame_width = frame_width
+        self.frame_height = frame_height
+        self.cal = cal or CalibrationConfig()
+        self.floor_region_config = floor_region_config or FloorRegionConfig()
+        self.refit_stride = refit_stride
+        self.max_samples = max_samples
+
+        self._ys: list[float] = []
+        self._heights: list[float] = []
+        self._widths: list[float] = []
+        self._ankle_xs: list[float] = []
+        self._ankle_ys: list[float] = []
+        self._new_since_fit = 0
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+
+        self._fit = ScenePerspectiveFit()
+        self._floor_region = FloorRegion()
+        self.size_stats = RollingPersonSizeStats()
+
+        # Real-time, per-reliable-sample audit log (one JSON line per
+        # sample) — the raw per-person record a live/RTSP deployment needs
+        # for manual inspection, since the stream may run for hours and
+        # could be killed without ever hitting the "stream ended" save path.
+        # Distinct from `save()`'s aggregate snapshot, and from the 30-sample
+        # window RollingPersonSizeStats actually uses to make its decision
+        # (see module docstring reference in add_sample below) — this file
+        # is bounded to the most recent `sample_log_max_rows` rows so a
+        # 24/7 camera doesn't grow it unbounded; older rows are dropped
+        # automatically. Seeded from the existing file (if any) so a
+        # restart doesn't blank the recent history to zero.
+        self._sample_log_path = None
+        self._sample_log_rows: deque[str] | None = None
+        if sample_log_dir is not None:
+            sample_log_dir = Path(sample_log_dir)
+            sample_log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            self._sample_log_path = sample_log_dir / f"{camera_id}_samples.jsonl"
+            self._sample_log_rows = deque(maxlen=sample_log_max_rows)
+            if self._sample_log_path.exists():
+                with open(self._sample_log_path) as f:
+                    for line in f:
+                        line = line.strip()
+                        if line:
+                            self._sample_log_rows.append(line)
+
+    def add_sample(
+        self,
+        bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float],
+        ankle_x: float | None,
+        ankle_y: float | None = None,
+        track_id: int | None = None,
+        frame_num: int | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        x1, y1, x2, y2 = bbox
+        width, height = x2 - x1, y2 - y1
+        self.size_stats.add_sample(width, height)
+
+        if self._sample_log_rows is not None:
+            record = {
+                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
+                "frame_num": frame_num,
+                "track_id": track_id,
+                "bbox_height": round(height, 2),
+                "bbox_width": round(width, 2),
+            }
+            # deque(maxlen=...) auto-evicts the oldest row once at capacity;
+            # rewriting the whole (bounded, small) file keeps disk state in
+            # sync with that eviction -- an append-only write can't drop
+            # old rows on its own.
+            self._sample_log_rows.append(json.dumps(record))
+            with open(self._sample_log_path, "w") as f:
+                f.write("\n".join(self._sample_log_rows) + "\n")
+
+        with self._lock:
+            self._ys.append(y2)
+            self._heights.append(height)
+            self._widths.append(width)
+            self._ankle_xs.append(ankle_x if ankle_x is not None else (x1 + x2) / 2)
+            self._ankle_ys.append(ankle_y if ankle_y is not None else y2)
+
+            if len(self._ys) > self.max_samples:
+                overflow = len(self._ys) - self.max_samples
+                del self._ys[:overflow]
+                del self._heights[:overflow]
+                del self._widths[:overflow]
+                del self._ankle_xs[:overflow]
+                del self._ankle_ys[:overflow]
+
+            self._new_since_fit += 1
+            if self._new_since_fit >= self.refit_stride:
+                self._refit_locked()
+                self._new_since_fit = 0
+
+    def _refit_locked(self) -> None:
+        """Refit the perspective regression. Caller must hold self._lock."""
+        n = len(self._ys)
+        if n < self.cal.min_samples_for_confidence:
+            return
+
+        ys = np.array(self._ys, dtype=np.float64)
+        heights = np.array(self._heights, dtype=np.float64)
+        widths = np.array(self._widths, dtype=np.float64)
+        ankle_xs = np.array(self._ankle_xs, dtype=np.float64)
+
+        coef_h_x, coef_h_y, intercept_h, r2 = _fit_plane_with_r2(ankle_xs, ys, heights)
+        coef_w_x, coef_w_y, intercept_w, _ = _fit_plane_with_r2(ankle_xs, ys, widths)
+
+        direction = "flat"
+        if abs(coef_h_y) > 1e-4:
+            x_corr = np.corrcoef(ankle_xs, ys)[0, 1] if n > 1 and np.std(ankle_xs) > 1e-6 else 0.0
+            if not np.isfinite(x_corr):
+                x_corr = 0.0
+            if x_corr > 0.2:
+                direction = "tilted_up_right"
+            elif x_corr < -0.2:
+                direction = "tilted_up_left"
+            else:
+                direction = "flat"
+
+        self._fit = ScenePerspectiveFit(
+            coef_h_x=coef_h_x, coef_h_y=coef_h_y, intercept_h=intercept_h,
+            coef_w_x=coef_w_x, coef_w_y=coef_w_y, intercept_w=intercept_w,
+            r_squared=r2, num_samples=n,
+        )
+        self._last_direction = direction
+        self._floor_region = self._compute_floor_region(np.array(self._ankle_ys, dtype=np.float64))
+
+    def _compute_floor_region(self, ankle_ys: np.ndarray) -> FloorRegion:
+        n = len(ankle_ys)
+        frc = self.floor_region_config
+        if n < frc.min_samples_for_confidence:
+            return FloorRegion(num_samples=n)
+
+        q25, q75 = np.percentile(ankle_ys, [25, 75])
+        iqr = max(float(q75 - q25), 1e-3)
+        median = float(np.median(ankle_ys))
+        half_width = frc.band_half_width_ratio * iqr
+        confidence = min(1.0, n / max(frc.full_confidence_samples, 1))
+        return FloorRegion(
+            band_low=float(median - half_width), band_high=float(median + half_width),
+            confidence=confidence, num_samples=n,
+        )
+
+    def build_profile(self) -> SceneProfile:
+        with self._lock:
+            fit = self._fit
+            floor_region = self._floor_region
+            n = len(self._ys)
+            direction = getattr(self, "_last_direction", "unknown")
+
+        if n >= self.cal.min_samples_for_confidence:
+            confidence = min(1.0, n / max(self.cal.full_confidence_samples, 1))
+        else:
+            confidence = 0.0
+        stats_snapshot = self.size_stats.snapshot(self.cal)
+
+        return SceneProfile(
+            camera_id=self.camera_id,
+            frame_width=self.frame_width,
+            frame_height=self.frame_height,
+            calibration_confidence=confidence,
+            perspective=fit,
+            size_stats=stats_snapshot,
+            dominant_floor_direction=direction if fit.is_valid else "unknown",
+            floor_region=floor_region,
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        """No-op: the per-sample audit log (if any) writes+closes its file
+        on every sample rather than holding an open handle, so there's
+        nothing left open to release. Kept for API stability."""
+
+    def save(self, directory: str | Path = "configs/scene_profiles") -> Path:
+        """Persist the current profile so future runs on this camera don't
+        need to recalibrate from scratch."""
+        directory = Path(directory)
+        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        path = directory / f"{self.camera_id}.json"
+        with open(path, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(self.build_profile().to_dict(), f, indent=2)
+        return path
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def load_seed(camera_id: str, directory: str | Path = "configs/scene_profiles") -> dict | None:
+        """Load a previously saved profile dict, if any, to seed logging/
+        display only (the builder still recalibrates from live samples;
+        this just avoids reporting "unavailable" for a camera already seen)."""
+        path = Path(directory) / f"{camera_id}.json"
+        if not path.exists():
+            return None
+        with open(path) as f:
+            return json.load(f)
+
+
+def _fit_plane_with_r2(
+    x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, z: np.ndarray
+) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
+    """Least-squares plane fit z = coef_x*x + coef_y*y + intercept, plus R^2
+    — the 2D generalization of the old single-variable line fit, since
+    expected bbox size genuinely depends on both image column and row for
+    a camera looking down at an angle, not row alone. Degrades gracefully
+    (falls back toward a row-only or constant fit) when there isn't enough
+    variation in x yet to constrain that term, rather than producing a
+    numerically unstable fit from an ill-conditioned system."""
+    n = len(x)
+    if n < 3:
+        return 0.0, 0.0, float(np.mean(z)) if n else 0.0, 0.0
+
+    design = np.column_stack([x, y, np.ones(n)])
+    if np.std(x) < 1e-6:
+        # No horizontal variation observed yet -- solving for coef_x would
+        # be numerically degenerate (a column of near-zero variance), so
+        # drop it and fit row-only instead of letting lstsq return a
+        # meaningless/unstable value for it.
+        design = design[:, 1:]
+        (coef_y, intercept), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(design, z, rcond=None)
+        coef_x = 0.0
+    else:
+        (coef_x, coef_y, intercept), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(design, z, rcond=None)
+
+    pred = coef_x * x + coef_y * y + intercept
+    ss_res = np.sum((z - pred) ** 2)
+    ss_tot = np.sum((z - np.mean(z)) ** 2)
+    r2 = 1.0 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot > 1e-9 else 0.0
+    return float(coef_x), float(coef_y), float(intercept), float(max(0.0, r2))

+"""Lightweight IoU-based multi-object tracker for edge deployment.
+
+No PyTorch or Ultralytics dependency — uses only numpy and scipy.
+Designed to replace BoT-SORT when running on edge devices with ONNX Runtime.
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment
+
+
+class SimpleTracker:
+    """IoU-based multi-object tracker using Hungarian algorithm.
+
+    Assigns persistent track IDs to bounding box detections across frames.
+    Uses Intersection-over-Union (IoU) for matching detections to existing tracks.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, iou_threshold: float = 0.3, max_lost: int = 30):
+        """Initialize tracker.
+
+        Args:
+            iou_threshold: Minimum IoU to match a detection to a track.
+            max_lost: Remove tracks not seen for this many frames.
+        """
+        self.iou_threshold = iou_threshold
+        self.max_lost = max_lost
+        self._next_id = 1
+        self._tracks: dict[int, dict] = {}  # id → {bbox, lost_count}
+
+    def update(self, bboxes: np.ndarray) -> list[int]:
+        """Update tracker with new detections and return track IDs.
+
+        Args:
+            bboxes: Array of shape (N, 4) with [x1, y1, x2, y2] per detection.
+
+        Returns:
+            List of track IDs (length N), one per input bbox.
+        """
+        if len(bboxes) == 0:
+            self._increment_lost()
+            self._remove_stale()
+            return []
+
+        bboxes = np.array(bboxes, dtype=np.float32)
+
+        if not self._tracks:
+            # First frame — create new tracks for all detections
+            track_ids = []
+            for bbox in bboxes:
+                tid = self._next_id
+                self._next_id += 1
+                self._tracks[tid] = {"bbox": bbox, "lost_count": 0}
+                track_ids.append(tid)
+            return track_ids
+
+        # Compute IoU matrix between existing tracks and new detections
+        track_ids_list = list(self._tracks.keys())
+        track_bboxes = np.array([self._tracks[tid]["bbox"] for tid in track_ids_list])
+        iou_matrix = self._compute_iou_matrix(track_bboxes, bboxes)
+
+        # Hungarian algorithm for optimal matching
+        cost_matrix = 1.0 - iou_matrix
+        row_indices, col_indices = linear_sum_assignment(cost_matrix)
+
+        # Assign matches
+        assigned_track_ids = [-1] * len(bboxes)
+        matched_tracks = set()
+        matched_detections = set()
+
+        for row, col in zip(row_indices, col_indices):
+            if iou_matrix[row, col] >= self.iou_threshold:
+                tid = track_ids_list[row]
+                assigned_track_ids[col] = tid
+                self._tracks[tid]["bbox"] = bboxes[col]
+                self._tracks[tid]["lost_count"] = 0
+                matched_tracks.add(tid)
+                matched_detections.add(col)
+
+        # Create new tracks for unmatched detections
+        for i in range(len(bboxes)):
+            if i not in matched_detections:
+                tid = self._next_id
+                self._next_id += 1
+                self._tracks[tid] = {"bbox": bboxes[i], "lost_count": 0}
+                assigned_track_ids[i] = tid
+
+        # Increment lost count for unmatched tracks
+        for tid in track_ids_list:
+            if tid not in matched_tracks:
+                self._tracks[tid]["lost_count"] += 1
+
+        self._remove_stale()
+
+        return assigned_track_ids
+
+    def _increment_lost(self):
+        """Increment lost count for all tracks (no detections this frame)."""
+        for tid in self._tracks:
+            self._tracks[tid]["lost_count"] += 1
+
+    def _remove_stale(self):
+        """Remove tracks not seen for max_lost frames."""
+        stale = [tid for tid, t in self._tracks.items() if t["lost_count"] > self.max_lost]
+        for tid in stale:
+            del self._tracks[tid]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _compute_iou_matrix(boxes_a: np.ndarray, boxes_b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Compute IoU between two sets of bounding boxes.
+
+        Args:
+            boxes_a: (M, 4) array of [x1, y1, x2, y2].
+            boxes_b: (N, 4) array of [x1, y1, x2, y2].
+
+        Returns:
+            (M, N) IoU matrix.
+        """
+        m, n = len(boxes_a), len(boxes_b)
+        iou = np.zeros((m, n), dtype=np.float32)
+
+        for i in range(m):
+            for j in range(n):
+                x1 = max(boxes_a[i, 0], boxes_b[j, 0])
+                y1 = max(boxes_a[i, 1], boxes_b[j, 1])
+                x2 = min(boxes_a[i, 2], boxes_b[j, 2])
+                y2 = min(boxes_a[i, 3], boxes_b[j, 3])
+
+                inter = max(0, x2 - x1) * max(0, y2 - y1)
+
+                area_a = (boxes_a[i, 2] - boxes_a[i, 0]) * (boxes_a[i, 3] - boxes_a[i, 1])
+                area_b = (boxes_b[j, 2] - boxes_b[j, 0]) * (boxes_b[j, 3] - boxes_b[j, 1])
+
+                union = area_a + area_b - inter
+                iou[i, j] = inter / union if union > 0 else 0.0
+
+        return iou
+
+    def reset(self):
+        """Reset all tracks."""
+        self._tracks.clear()
+        self._next_id = 1
+
+    @property
+    def active_count(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._tracks)

+"""Per-track temporal state machine with hysteresis.
+
+Three explicit states: NORMAL, POSSIBLE_MANDOWN, MANDOWN. A single
+anomalous frame can never trigger or clear an alert — transitions require
+several consecutive frames of consistent fusion evidence, so a track
+recovers back to NORMAL only after sustained normal-looking evidence too.
+
+MANDOWN covers both a falling transition and an already-lying person —
+whichever evidence (fall_motion_score or down_score/floor_proximity_score,
+via the fusion score) drives the escalation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum
+
+from src.config import StateMachineConfig
+
+
+class MandownState(str, Enum):
+    NORMAL = "NORMAL"
+    POSSIBLE_MANDOWN = "POSSIBLE_MANDOWN"
+    MANDOWN = "MANDOWN"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class StepResult:
+    state: MandownState
+    entered_mandown: bool  # True only on the frame that first confirms MANDOWN
+    recovered: bool        # True only on the frame that returns to NORMAL from a non-NORMAL state
+
+
+class TrackStateMachine:
+    """One instance per track_id. Call `step()` once per frame with that
+    frame's fusion-suggested tier ("NORMAL" | "POSSIBLE_MANDOWN" | "MANDOWN")."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config: StateMachineConfig | None = None):
+        self.config = config or StateMachineConfig()
+        self.state = MandownState.NORMAL
+        self._up_streak = 0
+        self._down_streak = 0
+
+    def step(self, suggested_tier: str) -> StepResult:
+        c = self.config
+        entered_mandown = False
+        recovered = False
+        is_up = suggested_tier in ("POSSIBLE_MANDOWN", "MANDOWN")
+
+        if self.state == MandownState.NORMAL:
+            self._up_streak = self._up_streak + 1 if is_up else 0
+            if self._up_streak >= c.frames_to_enter_possible:
+                self.state = MandownState.POSSIBLE_MANDOWN
+                self._up_streak = 0
+            self._down_streak = 0
+
+        elif self.state == MandownState.POSSIBLE_MANDOWN:
+            if is_up:
+                self._up_streak += 1
+                self._down_streak = 0
+            else:
+                self._down_streak += 1
+                self._up_streak = 0
+
+            if self._up_streak >= c.frames_to_confirm_mandown:
+                self.state = MandownState.MANDOWN
+                entered_mandown = True
+                self._up_streak = 0
+            elif self._down_streak >= c.frames_to_recover_normal:
+                self.state = MandownState.NORMAL
+                recovered = True
+                self._down_streak = 0
+
+        else:  # MANDOWN — sticky until sustained normal evidence
+            if suggested_tier == "NORMAL":
+                self._down_streak += 1
+            else:
+                self._down_streak = 0
+
+            if self._down_streak >= c.frames_to_recover_normal:
+                self.state = MandownState.NORMAL
+                recovered = True
+                self._down_streak = 0
+
+        return StepResult(state=self.state, entered_mandown=entered_mandown, recovered=recovered)
+
+    def on_gap(self, gap_frames: int, tolerance_frames: int) -> None:
+        """Call once when a track resumes after `gap_frames` of no detection
+        at all (before the next `step()`). Beyond `tolerance_frames`, hysteresis
+        progress-toward-a-transition is discarded — otherwise a long silent gap
+        could let stale pre-gap momentum finish confirming/recovering a
+        transition it didn't actually earn. `self.state` itself is untouched:
+        a confirmed MANDOWN stays MANDOWN through the gap, per the "temporary
+        pose failure must not immediately reset Mandown" requirement."""
+        if gap_frames > tolerance_frames:
+            self._up_streak = 0
+            self._down_streak = 0
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self.state = MandownState.NORMAL
+        self._up_streak = 0
+        self._down_streak = 0

+"""Per-track sliding window buffer management for temporal classification."""
+
+import logging
+from collections import deque
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from src.feature_extraction import FeatureVector
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class TrackState:
+    """State for a single tracked person."""
+
+    def __init__(self, track_id: int, window_size: int = 30):
+        self.track_id = track_id
+        self.window_size = window_size
+        self.features: deque[FeatureVector] = deque(maxlen=window_size)
+        self.last_seen_frame: int = 0
+        self.prev_cog_height: float | None = None
+        self.classification: str = "normal"
+        self.classification_confidence: float = 0.0
+        self.total_frames_seen: int = 0
+
+    def add_features(self, fv: FeatureVector, frame_num: int) -> None:
+        """Add a feature vector to this track's buffer."""
+        self.features.append(fv)
+        self.last_seen_frame = frame_num
+        self.prev_cog_height = fv.cog_height
+        self.total_frames_seen += 1
+
+    def get_sequence(self) -> np.ndarray | None:
+        """Get the feature sequence as a numpy array.
+
+        Returns:
+            Array of shape (window_size, NUM_FEATURES) if buffer is full,
+            None otherwise.
+        """
+        if len(self.features) < self.window_size:
+            return None
+        return np.array([fv.to_array() for fv in self.features], dtype=np.float32)
+
+    def is_ready(self) -> bool:
+        """Check if the buffer has enough frames for classification."""
+        return len(self.features) >= self.window_size
+
+    @property
+    def buffer_fill(self) -> float:
+        """Fraction of buffer that is filled (0.0 to 1.0)."""
+        return len(self.features) / self.window_size
+
+
+class TrackManager:
+    """Manages per-track sliding window buffers for all tracked persons.
+
+    Handles track creation, feature buffering, stale track cleanup,
+    and provides sequences ready for LSTM classification.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        window_size: int = 30,
+        stale_threshold: int = 90,
+    ):
+        """Initialize the track manager.
+
+        Args:
+            window_size: Number of frames to buffer per track for classification.
+            stale_threshold: Remove tracks not seen for this many frames.
+        """
+        self.window_size = window_size
+        self.stale_threshold = stale_threshold
+        self.tracks: dict[int, TrackState] = {}
+        self._total_tracks_created = 0
+
+    def update(self, track_id: int, features: FeatureVector, frame_num: int) -> None:
+        """Update a track with new features.
+
+        Creates the track if it doesn't exist.
+
+        Args:
+            track_id: BoT-SORT track ID.
+            features: Extracted features for this frame.
+            frame_num: Current frame number.
+        """
+        if track_id < 0:
+            return  # Skip untracked detections
+
+        if track_id not in self.tracks:
+            self.tracks[track_id] = TrackState(track_id, self.window_size)
+            self._total_tracks_created += 1
+            logger.debug(f"New track created: {track_id}")
+
+        self.tracks[track_id].add_features(features, frame_num)
+
+    def get_sequence(self, track_id: int) -> np.ndarray | None:
+        """Get the feature sequence for a track.
+
+        Returns:
+            Array of shape (window_size, NUM_FEATURES) if ready, None otherwise.
+        """
+        if track_id not in self.tracks:
+            return None
+        return self.tracks[track_id].get_sequence()
+
+    def get_prev_cog_height(self, track_id: int) -> float | None:
+        """Get the previous CoG height for velocity computation."""
+        if track_id not in self.tracks:
+            return None
+        return self.tracks[track_id].prev_cog_height
+
+    def set_classification(
+        self, track_id: int, classification: str, confidence: float
+    ) -> None:
+        """Set the classification result for a track."""
+        if track_id in self.tracks:
+            self.tracks[track_id].classification = classification
+            self.tracks[track_id].classification_confidence = confidence
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Training loop for the fall detection LSTM classifier."""
+
+import json
+import logging
+import random
+import sys
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from sklearn.metrics import f1_score
+from sklearn.utils.class_weight import compute_class_weight
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
+
+from models.fall_detector import FallDetector
+from src.dataset import create_dataloaders, load_splits
+
+logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s: %(message)s")
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def set_seed(seed: int = 42):
+    """Set all random seeds for reproducibility."""
+    random.seed(seed)
+    np.random.seed(seed)
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
+    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
+    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
+
+
+def train_one_epoch(
+    model: nn.Module,
+    dataloader,
+    criterion: nn.Module,
+    optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
+    device: torch.device,
+    max_grad_norm: float = 1.0,
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Train for one epoch. Returns (avg_loss, accuracy)."""
+    model.train()
+    total_loss = 0.0
+    correct = 0
+    total = 0
+
+    for X_batch, y_batch in dataloader:
+        X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
+
+        optimizer.zero_grad()
+        logits = model(X_batch)
+        loss = criterion(logits, y_batch)
+        loss.backward()
+        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_grad_norm)
+        optimizer.step()
+
+        total_loss += loss.item() * len(y_batch)
+        preds = logits.argmax(dim=1)
+        correct += (preds == y_batch).sum().item()
+        total += len(y_batch)
+
+    return total_loss / total, correct / total
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def evaluate(
+    model: nn.Module,
+    dataloader,
+    criterion: nn.Module,
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
+    """Evaluate model. Returns (avg_loss, accuracy, macro_f1)."""
+    model.eval()
+    total_loss = 0.0
+    all_preds = []
+    all_labels = []
+
+    for X_batch, y_batch in dataloader:
+        X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
+        logits = model(X_batch)
+        loss = criterion(logits, y_batch)
+
+        total_loss += loss.item() * len(y_batch)
+        all_preds.extend(logits.argmax(dim=1).cpu().numpy())
+        all_labels.extend(y_batch.cpu().numpy())
+
+    total = len(all_labels)
+    accuracy = sum(p == label for p, label in zip(all_preds, all_labels)) / total
+    macro_f1 = f1_score(all_labels, all_preds, average="macro")
+
+    return total_loss / total, accuracy, macro_f1
+
+
+def train(
+    data_dir: str = "data/splits",
+    checkpoint_dir: str = "models/checkpoints",
+    epochs: int = 100,
+    batch_size: int = 64,
+    lr: float = 1e-3,
+    weight_decay: float = 1e-4,
+    patience: int = 15,
+    seed: int = 42,
+    device_name: str | None = None,
+):
+    """Full training pipeline."""
+    set_seed(seed)
+
+    # Device
+    if device_name is None:
+        device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
+    else:
+        device = torch.device(device_name)
+    logger.info(f"Device: {device}")
+
+    # Data
+    logger.info(f"Loading data from {data_dir}...")
+    splits = load_splits(data_dir)
+    loaders = create_dataloaders(splits, batch_size=batch_size, num_workers=0)
+
+    logger.info(
+        f"Train: {len(splits['train'])}, Val: {len(splits['val'])}, Test: {len(splits['test'])}"
+    )
+
+    # Compute class weights
+    y_train = splits["train"].y.numpy()
+    classes = np.unique(y_train)
+    weights = compute_class_weight("balanced", classes=classes, y=y_train)
+    class_weights = torch.FloatTensor(weights).to(device)
+    logger.info(f"Class weights: {dict(zip(classes.tolist(), [f'{w:.3f}' for w in weights]))}")
+
+    # Model
+    model = FallDetector().to(device)
+    param_count = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
+    logger.info(f"Model parameters: {param_count:,}")
+
+    # Training setup
+    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights)
+    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=weight_decay)
+    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(
+        optimizer, mode="min", patience=5, factor=0.5
+    )
+
+    # Training loop
+    checkpoint_path = Path(checkpoint_dir)
+    checkpoint_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    best_val_loss = float("inf")
+    best_epoch = 0
+    epochs_no_improve = 0
+    history = []
+    start_time = time.time()
+
+    logger.info(f"\nStarting training for up to {epochs} epochs...")
+    logger.info("-" * 80)
+
+    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
+        # Train
+        train_loss, train_acc = train_one_epoch(
+            model, loaders["train"], criterion, optimizer, device
+        )
+
+        # Validate
+        val_loss, val_acc, val_f1 = evaluate(model, loaders["val"], criterion, device)
+
+        # Scheduler step
+        scheduler.step(val_loss)
+        current_lr = optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"]
+
+        # Log
+        history.append({
+            "epoch": epoch,
+            "train_loss": train_loss,
+            "train_acc": train_acc,
+            "val_loss": val_loss,
+            "val_acc": val_acc,
+            "val_f1": val_f1,
+            "lr": current_lr,
+        })
+
+        logger.info(
+            f"Epoch {epoch:3d}/{epochs} | "
+            f"Train Loss: {train_loss:.4f} Acc: {train_acc:.4f} | "
+            f"Val Loss: {val_loss:.4f} Acc: {val_acc:.4f} F1: {val_f1:.4f} | "
+            f"LR: {current_lr:.6f}"
+        )
+
+        # Checkpointing
+        if val_loss < best_val_loss:
+            best_val_loss = val_loss
+            best_epoch = epoch
+            epochs_no_improve = 0
+            torch.save({
+                "epoch": epoch,
+                "model_state_dict": model.state_dict(),
+                "optimizer_state_dict": optimizer.state_dict(),
+                "val_loss": val_loss,
+                "val_acc": val_acc,
+                "val_f1": val_f1,
+            }, checkpoint_path / "best.pth")
+        else:
+            epochs_no_improve += 1
+
+        # Early stopping
+        if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
+            logger.info(f"\nEarly stopping at epoch {epoch} (no improvement for {patience} epochs)")
+            break
+
+    training_time = time.time() - start_time
+
+    # Save last checkpoint
+    torch.save({
+        "epoch": epoch,
+        "model_state_dict": model.state_dict(),
+        "optimizer_state_dict": optimizer.state_dict(),
+        "val_loss": val_loss,
+        "val_acc": val_acc,
+    }, checkpoint_path / "last.pth")
+
+    # Final evaluation on test set
+    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 80)
+    logger.info("Final evaluation on test set...")
+
+    # Load best model
+    best_ckpt = torch.load(checkpoint_path / "best.pth", map_location=device, weights_only=False)
+    model.load_state_dict(best_ckpt["model_state_dict"])
+
+    test_loss, test_acc, test_f1 = evaluate(model, loaders["test"], criterion, device)
+    logger.info(f"Test Loss: {test_loss:.4f} | Acc: {test_acc:.4f} | Macro F1: {test_f1:.4f}")
+
+    # Per-class metrics
+    model.eval()
+    all_preds, all_labels = [], []
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for X_batch, y_batch in loaders["test"]:
+            X_batch = X_batch.to(device)
+            preds = model(X_batch).argmax(dim=1).cpu().numpy()
+            all_preds.extend(preds)
+            all_labels.extend(y_batch.numpy())
+
+    from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix
+
+    class_names = ["normal", "falling", "fallen"]
+    report = classification_report(all_labels, all_preds, target_names=class_names)
+    cm = confusion_matrix(all_labels, all_preds)
+
+    logger.info(f"\nClassification Report:\n{report}")
+    logger.info(f"Confusion Matrix:\n{cm}")
+
+    # Save training report
+    report_dict = classification_report(
+        all_labels, all_preds, target_names=class_names, output_dict=True
+    )
+    training_report = {
+        "training_time_seconds": round(training_time, 1),
+        "total_epochs": epoch,
+        "best_epoch": best_epoch,
+        "best_val_loss": round(best_val_loss, 4),
+        "test_accuracy": round(test_acc, 4),
+        "test_macro_f1": round(test_f1, 4),
+        "per_class_metrics": report_dict,
+        "confusion_matrix": cm.tolist(),
+        "history": history,
+    }
+
+    report_path = checkpoint_path / "training_report.json"
+    with open(report_path, "w") as f:
+        json.dump(training_report, f, indent=2, default=str)
+    logger.info(f"\nTraining report saved to {report_path}")
+
+    logger.info(f"\nTraining complete in {training_time:.1f}s")
+    logger.info(f"Best model (epoch {best_epoch}) saved to {checkpoint_path / 'best.pth'}")
+
+    return model, training_report
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    train()

+"""Drawing helpers, color maps, and visualization utilities."""
+
+import cv2
+import numpy as np
+
+# COCO keypoint skeleton connections (pairs of keypoint indices)
+COCO_SKELETON = [
+    (0, 1), (0, 2),      # nose → eyes
+    (1, 3), (2, 4),      # eyes → ears
+    (5, 6),               # shoulder → shoulder
+    (5, 7), (7, 9),      # left arm
+    (6, 8), (8, 10),     # right arm
+    (5, 11), (6, 12),    # torso
+    (11, 12),             # hip → hip
+    (11, 13), (13, 15),  # left leg
+    (12, 14), (14, 16),  # right leg
+]
+
+# COCO keypoint names (17 keypoints)
+COCO_KEYPOINT_NAMES = [
+    "nose", "left_eye", "right_eye", "left_ear", "right_ear",
+    "left_shoulder", "right_shoulder", "left_elbow", "right_elbow",
+    "left_wrist", "right_wrist", "left_hip", "right_hip",
+    "left_knee", "right_knee", "left_ankle", "right_ankle",
+]
+
+# Color definitions (BGR format for OpenCV)
+COLOR_GREEN = (0, 255, 0)
+COLOR_RED = (0, 0, 255)
+COLOR_ORANGE = (0, 165, 255)
+COLOR_WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
+COLOR_BLACK = (0, 0, 0)
+COLOR_YELLOW = (0, 255, 255)
+COLOR_BLUE = (255, 0, 0)
+
+# Status colors for different states
+STATUS_COLORS = {
+    "normal": COLOR_GREEN,
+    "falling": COLOR_ORANGE,
+    "fallen": COLOR_RED,
+}
+
+
+def draw_skeleton(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    keypoints: np.ndarray,
+    color: tuple[int, int, int] = COLOR_GREEN,
+    confidence_threshold: float = 0.3,
+    thickness: int = 2,
+    point_radius: int = 4,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw skeleton on frame from COCO keypoints.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        keypoints: Array of shape (17, 3) with [x, y, confidence].
+        color: BGR color for the skeleton.
+        confidence_threshold: Minimum confidence to draw a keypoint/connection.
+        thickness: Line thickness.
+        point_radius: Radius of keypoint circles.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with skeleton drawn.
+    """
+    if keypoints is None or len(keypoints) == 0:
+        return frame
+
+    # Draw connections
+    for i, j in COCO_SKELETON:
+        if i >= len(keypoints) or j >= len(keypoints):
+            continue
+        if keypoints[i][2] < confidence_threshold or keypoints[j][2] < confidence_threshold:
+            continue
+        pt1 = (int(keypoints[i][0]), int(keypoints[i][1]))
+        pt2 = (int(keypoints[j][0]), int(keypoints[j][1]))
+        cv2.line(frame, pt1, pt2, color, thickness)
+
+    # Draw keypoints
+    for kp in keypoints:
+        if kp[2] < confidence_threshold:
+            continue
+        center = (int(kp[0]), int(kp[1]))
+        cv2.circle(frame, center, point_radius, color, -1)
+
+    return frame
+
+
+def draw_bbox(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    bbox: tuple[int, int, int, int],
+    color: tuple[int, int, int] = COLOR_GREEN,
+    thickness: int = 2,
+    label: str | None = None,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw bounding box with optional label.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        bbox: (x1, y1, x2, y2) coordinates.
+        color: BGR color.
+        thickness: Line thickness.
+        label: Optional text label above the box.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with bbox drawn.
+    """
+    x1, y1, x2, y2 = [int(v) for v in bbox]
+    cv2.rectangle(frame, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), color, thickness)
+
+    if label:
+        font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
+        font_scale = 0.6
+        (text_w, text_h), baseline = cv2.getTextSize(label, font, font_scale, 1)
+        # Draw label above bbox if room, otherwise below top edge
+        label_above = y1 - text_h - baseline - 4 >= 0
+        if label_above:
+            cv2.rectangle(
+                frame, (x1, y1 - text_h - baseline - 4), (x1 + text_w, y1), color, -1
+            )
+            cv2.putText(frame, label, (x1, y1 - baseline - 2), font, font_scale, COLOR_BLACK, 1)
+        else:
+            cv2.rectangle(
+                frame, (x1, y1), (x1 + text_w, y1 + text_h + baseline + 4), color, -1
+            )
+            cv2.putText(
+                frame, label, (x1, y1 + text_h + 2), font, font_scale, COLOR_BLACK, 1
+            )
+
+    return frame
+
+
+def draw_alert(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    text: str,
+    position: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
+    color: tuple[int, int, int] = COLOR_RED,
+    font_scale: float = 1.2,
+    thickness: int = 3,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw an alert text on the frame with background.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        text: Alert text to display.
+        position: (x, y) position. If None, centered at top.
+        color: BGR text color.
+        font_scale: Font size scale.
+        thickness: Text thickness.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with alert drawn.
+    """
+    font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
+    (text_w, text_h), baseline = cv2.getTextSize(text, font, font_scale, thickness)
+
+    if position is None:
+        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
+        x = (w - text_w) // 2
+        y = text_h + 20
+    else:
+        x, y = position
+
+    # Semi-transparent background (ROI-based for performance)
+    padding = 10
+    h_frame, w_frame = frame.shape[:2]
+    rx1 = max(0, x - padding)
+    ry1 = max(0, y - text_h - padding)
+    rx2 = min(w_frame, x + text_w + padding)
+    ry2 = min(h_frame, y + baseline + padding)
+    roi = frame[ry1:ry2, rx1:rx2].copy()
+    cv2.rectangle(frame, (rx1, ry1), (rx2, ry2), COLOR_BLACK, -1)
+    cv2.addWeighted(frame[ry1:ry2, rx1:rx2], 0.6, roi, 0.4, 0, frame[ry1:ry2, rx1:rx2])
+
+    cv2.putText(frame, text, (x, y), font, font_scale, color, thickness)
+    return frame
+
+
+def draw_fall_banner(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    text: str,
+    color: tuple[int, int, int] = COLOR_RED,
+    timestamp: str | None = None,
+    font_scale: float = 1.0,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw a bold, black-outlined alert label top-left with a timestamp top-right.
+
+    Matches the look of typical CCTV/surveillance overlay alerts (e.g. a
+    "Missing PPE" banner) rather than the centered semi-transparent alert box.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        text: Alert label, e.g. "Fall Alert: Falling".
+        color: BGR color for the label text.
+        timestamp: Optional short timestamp string drawn in the top-right corner.
+        font_scale: Base font scale, typically resolution-scaled.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with the banner drawn.
+    """
+    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
+    font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
+    thickness = max(2, int(2 * font_scale))
+    outline_thickness = thickness + 3
+
+    x, y = 12, int(30 * font_scale) + 10
+    cv2.putText(frame, text, (x, y), font, font_scale, COLOR_BLACK, outline_thickness, cv2.LINE_AA)
+    cv2.putText(frame, text, (x, y), font, font_scale, color, thickness, cv2.LINE_AA)
+
+    if timestamp:
+        ts_font_scale = 0.6 * font_scale
+        ts_thickness = max(1, int(1.5 * font_scale))
+        (tw, _th), _baseline = cv2.getTextSize(timestamp, font, ts_font_scale, ts_thickness)
+        tx = w - tw - 12
+        ty = y
+        cv2.putText(
+            frame, timestamp, (tx, ty), font, ts_font_scale,
+            COLOR_BLACK, ts_thickness + 2, cv2.LINE_AA,
+        )
+        cv2.putText(
+            frame, timestamp, (tx, ty), font, ts_font_scale,
+            COLOR_WHITE, ts_thickness, cv2.LINE_AA,
+        )
+
+    return frame
+
+
+def draw_mandown_banner(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    text: str = "MANDOWN",
+    color: tuple[int, int, int] = COLOR_RED,
+    font_scale: float = 1.0,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw a plain solid-black banner chip, top-left, with bold text —
+    e.g. "MANDOWN". Matches common CCTV/surveillance overlay alert style
+    (solid dark background behind bold colored text), deliberately minimal
+    — no timestamp, duration, or other detail folded in.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        text: Banner text, e.g. "MANDOWN".
+        color: BGR text color.
+        font_scale: Base font scale, typically resolution-scaled.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with the banner drawn.
+    """
+    font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
+    font_scale = font_scale * 2.0  # doubled — the original size read too small
+    thickness = max(2, int(2 * font_scale))
+    padding = int(10 * font_scale)
+
+    (tw, th), baseline = cv2.getTextSize(text, font, font_scale, thickness)
+    x1, y1 = 0, 0
+    x2, y2 = tw + padding * 2, th + baseline + padding * 2
+
+    cv2.rectangle(frame, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), COLOR_BLACK, -1)
+    # Text origin is the baseline; the glyph block spans `th` (ascent) above
+    # it and `baseline` (descent) below it. Box height is th+baseline+2*
+    # padding, so placing the baseline at padding+th centers that block
+    # exactly, with equal black margin above and below — the previous
+    # `y2 - baseline - padding//2` placement left extra space on top.
+    cv2.putText(
+        frame, text, (x1 + padding, padding + th),
+        font, font_scale, color, thickness, cv2.LINE_AA,
+    )
+
+    return frame
+
+
+def draw_status_bar(
+    frame: np.ndarray,
+    frame_num: int,
+    total_frames: int | None,
+    fps: float,
+    persons_tracked: int,
+    falls_detected: int,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Draw a status bar at the bottom of the frame.
+
+    Args:
+        frame: BGR image (modified in place).
+        frame_num: Current frame number.
+        total_frames: Total number of frames in video, or None for a live stream.
+        fps: Processing FPS.
+        persons_tracked: Number of persons currently tracked.
+        falls_detected: Total falls detected so far.
+
+    Returns:
+        The frame with status bar drawn.
+    """
+    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
+    bar_height = 30
+    y_start = h - bar_height
+
+    # Semi-transparent black bar (ROI-based for performance)
+    roi = frame[y_start:h, 0:w].copy()
+    cv2.rectangle(frame, (0, y_start), (w, h), COLOR_BLACK, -1)
+    cv2.addWeighted(frame[y_start:h, 0:w], 0.7, roi, 0.3, 0, frame[y_start:h, 0:w])
+
+    # Status text
+    if total_frames:
+        progress = frame_num / max(total_frames, 1) * 100
+        frame_info = f"Frame: {frame_num}/{total_frames} ({progress:.0f}%)"
+    else:
+        frame_info = f"Frame: {frame_num} (LIVE)"
+    status = (

+"""Video reading and writing utilities with proper resource management."""
+
+import logging
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import cv2
+import numpy as np
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {".mp4", ".avi", ".mov", ".mkv"}
+
+CODEC_MAP = {
+    ".mp4": "mp4v",
+    ".avi": "XVID",
+    ".mov": "mp4v",
+    ".mkv": "mp4v",
+}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class VideoMetadata:
+    """Metadata extracted from a video file."""
+
+    width: int
+    height: int
+    fps: float
+    total_frames: int
+    duration_seconds: float
+    codec: str
+
+
+def validate_video_path(path: str | Path, must_exist: bool = True) -> Path:
+    """Validate a video file path.
+
+    Args:
+        path: Path to the video file.
+        must_exist: If True, verify the file exists.
+
+    Returns:
+        Validated Path object.
+
+    Raises:
+        FileNotFoundError: If must_exist and file doesn't exist.
+        ValueError: If extension is unsupported.
+    """
+    path = Path(path)
+    if must_exist and not path.exists():
+        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Video file not found: {path}")
+    if path.suffix.lower() not in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Unsupported video format '{path.suffix}'. "
+            f"Supported: {', '.join(sorted(SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS))}"
+        )
+    return path
+
+
+class VideoReader:
+    """Context manager for reading video files frame by frame.
+
+    Usage:
+        with VideoReader("input.mp4") as reader:
+            for frame_num, frame in reader:
+                process(frame)
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str | Path):
+        self.path = validate_video_path(path, must_exist=True)
+        self._cap: cv2.VideoCapture | None = None
+        self._metadata: VideoMetadata | None = None
+        self._frame_num = 0
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> "VideoReader":
+        self._cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(self.path))
+        if not self._cap.isOpened():
+            raise IOError(f"Failed to open video file: {self.path}")
+
+        width = int(self._cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH))
+        height = int(self._cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))
+        fps = self._cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)
+        total_frames = int(self._cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
+        fourcc = int(self._cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FOURCC))
+        codec = "".join([chr((fourcc >> 8 * i) & 0xFF) for i in range(4)])
+
+        if fps <= 0:
+            fps = 30.0  # Fallback for videos with missing FPS metadata
+
+        if total_frames <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Video has no frames: {self.path}")
+
+        duration = total_frames / fps if fps > 0 else 0.0
+
+        self._metadata = VideoMetadata(
+            width=width,
+            height=height,
+            fps=fps,
+            total_frames=total_frames,
+            duration_seconds=duration,
+            codec=codec,
+        )
+        self._frame_num = 0
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
+        if self._cap is not None:
+            self._cap.release()
+            self._cap = None
+        return False
+
+    def __iter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    def __next__(self) -> tuple[int, np.ndarray]:
+        if self._cap is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("VideoReader not opened. Use as context manager.")
+        ret, frame = self._cap.read()
+        if not ret:
+            raise StopIteration
+        frame_num = self._frame_num
+        self._frame_num += 1
+        return frame_num, frame
+
+    @property
+    def metadata(self) -> VideoMetadata:
+        if self._metadata is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("VideoReader not opened. Use as context manager.")
+        return self._metadata
+
+
+class VideoWriter:
+    """Context manager for writing video files.
+
+    Usage:
+        with VideoWriter("output.mp4", width=1920, height=1080, fps=30.0) as writer:
+            writer.write(frame)
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, width: int, height: int, fps: float):
+        self.path = validate_video_path(path, must_exist=False)
+        self.width = width
+        self.height = height
+        self.fps = fps
+        self._writer: cv2.VideoWriter | None = None
+        self._frame_count = 0
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> "VideoWriter":
+        os.makedirs(self.path.parent, exist_ok=True)
+
+        codec_str = CODEC_MAP.get(self.path.suffix.lower(), "mp4v")
+        fourcc = cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*codec_str)
+
+        self._writer = cv2.VideoWriter(
+            str(self.path), fourcc, self.fps, (self.width, self.height)
+        )
+        if not self._writer.isOpened():
+            raise IOError(f"Failed to create video writer for: {self.path}")
+
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
+        if self._writer is not None:
+            self._writer.release()
+            self._writer = None
+
+        # Convert to H.264 for browser/app compatibility
+        if exc_type is None and self._frame_count > 0:
+            self._convert_to_h264()
+
+        return False
+
+    def _convert_to_h264(self):
+        """Convert output video to H.264 codec using ffmpeg for browser compatibility."""
+        if not shutil.which("ffmpeg"):
+            logger.warning("ffmpeg not found, skipping H.264 conversion")
+            return
+
+        tmp_path = self.path.with_suffix(".tmp.mp4")
+        try:
+            subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    "ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(self.path),
+                    "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "fast", "-crf", "23",
+                    "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-an",
+                    str(tmp_path),
+                ],
+                capture_output=True,
+                timeout=300,
+            )
+            if tmp_path.exists() and tmp_path.stat().st_size > 0:
+                tmp_path.replace(self.path)
+                logger.debug(f"Converted to H.264: {self.path}")
+            else:
+                logger.warning("H.264 conversion produced empty file, keeping original")
+                if tmp_path.exists():
+                    tmp_path.unlink()
+        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as e:
+            logger.warning(f"H.264 conversion failed: {e}, keeping original")
+            if tmp_path.exists():
+                tmp_path.unlink()
+
+    def write(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> None:
+        """Write a single frame to the output video."""
+        if self._writer is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("VideoWriter not opened. Use as context manager.")
+
+        if frame.shape[1] != self.width or frame.shape[0] != self.height:
+            logger.warning(
+                f"Frame size ({frame.shape[1]}x{frame.shape[0]}) doesn't match "
+                f"writer size ({self.width}x{self.height}). Resizing."
+            )
+            frame = cv2.resize(frame, (self.width, self.height))
+
+        self._writer.write(frame)
+        self._frame_count += 1
+
+    @property
+    def frame_count(self) -> int:
+        return self._frame_count
+
+
+def format_timestamp(frame_num: int, fps: float) -> str:
+    """Convert frame number to HH:MM:SS.ms timestamp."""
+    if fps <= 0 or frame_num < 0:
+        return "00:00:00.000"
+    total_seconds = frame_num / fps
+    hours = int(total_seconds // 3600)
+    minutes = int((total_seconds % 3600) // 60)
+    seconds = total_seconds % 60
+    return f"{hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{seconds:06.3f}"
+
+
+def format_short_timestamp(frame_num: int, fps: float) -> str:
+    """Compact M:SS timestamp for on-frame overlays (e.g. '0:37')."""
+    if fps <= 0 or frame_num < 0:
+        return "0:00"
+    total_seconds = int(frame_num / fps)
+    minutes, seconds = divmod(total_seconds, 60)
+    return f"{minutes}:{seconds:02d}"
+
+
+def format_duration(seconds: float) -> str:
+    """Format duration in seconds to HH:MM:SS.s string."""
+    if seconds < 0:
+        return "00:00:00"
+    hours = int(seconds // 3600)
+    minutes = int((seconds % 3600) // 60)
+    secs = int(seconds % 60)
+    return f"{hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{secs:02d}"
+
+
+class ImageSequenceReader:
+    """Context manager for reading a folder of numbered images as a video.
+
+    Supports datasets like UR Fall that store frames as individual PNG/JPG files.
+
+    Usage:
+        with ImageSequenceReader("path/to/frames/", fps=30.0) as reader:
+            for frame_num, frame in reader:
+                process(frame)
+    """
+
+    IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = {".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".bmp"}
+
+    def __init__(self, directory: str | Path, fps: float = 30.0):
+        self.directory = Path(directory)
+        self.fps = fps
+        self._image_paths: list[Path] = []
+        self._metadata: VideoMetadata | None = None
+        self._index = 0
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> "ImageSequenceReader":
+        if not self.directory.exists() or not self.directory.is_dir():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Image sequence directory not found: {self.directory}")
+
+        # Collect and sort image files
+        self._image_paths = sorted(
+            f for f in self.directory.iterdir()
+            if f.suffix.lower() in self.IMAGE_EXTENSIONS
+        )
+
+        if not self._image_paths:
+            raise ValueError(f"No image files found in: {self.directory}")
+
+        # Read first image to get dimensions
+        first_frame = cv2.imread(str(self._image_paths[0]))
+        if first_frame is None:
+            raise IOError(f"Failed to read first image: {self._image_paths[0]}")
+
+        height, width = first_frame.shape[:2]
+        total_frames = len(self._image_paths)
+        duration = total_frames / self.fps if self.fps > 0 else 0.0
+
+        self._metadata = VideoMetadata(
+            width=width,
+            height=height,
+            fps=self.fps,
+            total_frames=total_frames,
+            duration_seconds=duration,
+            codec="PNG",
+        )
+        self._index = 0
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
+        self._image_paths = []
+        return False
+
+    def __iter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    def __next__(self) -> tuple[int, np.ndarray]:
+        if self._index >= len(self._image_paths):
+            raise StopIteration
+
+        img_path = self._image_paths[self._index]
+        frame = cv2.imread(str(img_path))
+        if frame is None:
+            logger.warning(f"Failed to read image {img_path}, skipping")
+            self._index += 1
+            return self.__next__()
+
+        frame_num = self._index
+        self._index += 1
+        return frame_num, frame
+
+    @property
+    def metadata(self) -> VideoMetadata:
+        if self._metadata is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("ImageSequenceReader not opened. Use as context manager.")
+        return self._metadata

+"""V3 Phase 8: already-lying-at-start integration tests.
+
+Wires the REAL component chain (base+extended feature extraction -> feature
+scorer -> evidence fusion -> temporal state machine) exactly as
+`pipeline.py::_process_frame` does per person, but with a static "already
+lying" posture fed from frame 0 of a brand-new track — no prior standing
+history, no fall velocity/acceleration, and critically, the LSTM is
+simulated cold (`lstm_mandown_prob=0.0` throughout, as if its 30-frame
+buffer never fills or it's simply wrong) to prove the geometric/floor
+evidence alone is sufficient, per the V3 requirement.
+
+This is UNIT/INTEGRATION TESTED with synthetic keypoints — not real-video
+validated. Real footage validated only the "back-ish" lying orientation
+that happened to appear in the available test videos; side/prone/diagonal
+orientations have no real footage available this session. See
+MANDOWN_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md for the explicit UNIT TESTED vs REAL
+VIDEO VALIDATED distinction.
+"""
+
+import math
+from collections import deque
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from src.config import FeatureMandownConfig, FusionConfig, HipDropConfig, KneelingConfig, StateMachineConfig
+from src.feature_extraction import ExtendedFeatureExtractor, FeatureExtractor
+from src.feature_mandown import FeatureMandownScorer
+from src.fusion import EvidenceFusion
+from src.mandown_track_context import MandownTrackContext
+from src.state_machine import MandownState, TrackStateMachine
+
+FRAME_W, FRAME_H = 640, 480
+
+
+def _kps(overrides: dict) -> np.ndarray:
+    kps = np.zeros((17, 3), dtype=np.float32)
+    kps[:] = [FRAME_W / 2, FRAME_H / 2, 0.9]
+    for idx, val in overrides.items():
+        kps[idx] = val
+    return kps
+
+
+def standing_keypoints() -> np.ndarray:
+    return _kps({
+        0: (320, 60, 0.95),
+        5: (295, 140, 0.9), 6: (345, 140, 0.9),
+        11: (300, 280, 0.9), 12: (340, 280, 0.9),
+        13: (300, 370, 0.9), 14: (340, 370, 0.9),
+        15: (300, 450, 0.9), 16: (340, 450, 0.9),

+
+
+def supine_lying_keypoints() -> np.ndarray:

+        5: (200, 300, 0.9), 6: (200, 320, 0.9),
+        11: (380, 300, 0.9), 12: (380, 320, 0.9),
+        13: (480, 300, 0.9), 14: (480, 320, 0.9),

+    """Face-down lying — geometrically similar 2D layout to supine (COCO
+    2D keypoints don't distinguish face-up/face-down orientation on their
+    own); included for explicit test coverage per the spec's request."""
+    return _kps({
+        0: (130, 310, 0.85),
+        5: (210, 305, 0.9), 6: (210, 325, 0.9),
+        11: (390, 305, 0.9), 12: (390, 325, 0.9),

+    "genuinely lying with a bent knee" exception."""
+    return _kps({
+        0: (150, 300, 0.85),
+        5: (230, 295, 0.9), 6: (230, 315, 0.85),

+    when the body axis isn't image-horizontal."""
+    return _kps({

+        5: (220, 240, 0.9), 6: (210, 260, 0.9),

+
+class _StaticTrackSimulator:
+    """Feeds identical keypoints frame after frame through the real
+    base+extended feature -> scorer -> fusion -> state-machine chain,
+    simulating a track that starts already in this posture with the LSTM
+    cold (0.0) the entire time."""
+
+    def __init__(self, expected_height_fn=None, floor_contact_score=0.0, hip_drop_config=None):
+        self.base_extractor = FeatureExtractor()
+        self.ext_extractor = ExtendedFeatureExtractor()
+        self.scorer = FeatureMandownScorer(FeatureMandownConfig(), KneelingConfig())
+        self.fusion = EvidenceFusion(FusionConfig())
+        self.state_machine = TrackStateMachine(StateMachineConfig())
+        self.expected_height_fn = expected_height_fn
+        # In real deployment, floor-region calibration and standing-height
+        # calibration come from the same scene-profiling pipeline (both need
+        # enough reliable samples) -- a test wiring one on should usually
+        # wire the other on too, rather than leaving this at its default-0.0
+        # "uncalibrated" reading while claiming height calibration is active.
+        self.floor_contact_score = floor_contact_score
+        # V4.4: a real MandownTrackContext, not a re-implementation -- this
+        # is exactly what carries last_standing_cog_height/hip_drop_evidence
+        # in the real pipeline, so using it here keeps this simulator
+        # genuinely representative rather than a parallel approximation
+        # that could silently drift from the real logic.
+        self.hip_drop_config = hip_drop_config or HipDropConfig()
+        self.ctx = MandownTrackContext(history_maxlen=30)
+
+        self.base_history = deque(maxlen=30)
+        self.ext_history = deque(maxlen=30)
+        self.prev_ext = None
+        self.prev_cog_x = None
+        self.prev_vertical_velocity = None
+
+    def step(self, keypoints: np.ndarray, bbox: tuple, lstm_mandown_prob: float = 0.0) -> MandownState:
+        prev_cog = self.base_history[-1].cog_height if self.base_history else None
+        base = self.base_extractor.extract(keypoints, bbox, FRAME_H, prev_cog)
+        self.base_history.append(base)
+
+        ext = self.ext_extractor.extract(
+            keypoints, bbox, FRAME_W, FRAME_H,
+            prev=self.prev_ext, prev_cog_x=self.prev_cog_x,
+            vertical_velocity_now=base.vertical_velocity,
+            prev_vertical_velocity=self.prev_vertical_velocity,
+            expected_height_fn=self.expected_height_fn,
+        )
+        self.ext_history.append(ext)
+        self.prev_ext = ext
+        self.prev_cog_x = self.ext_extractor.cog_x(keypoints, bbox)
+        self.prev_vertical_velocity = base.vertical_velocity
+
+        hip_drop_evidence = self.ctx.hip_drop_evidence(base.cog_height, self.hip_drop_config)
+        # torso_angle alone isn't enough -- see pipeline.py's identical
+        # check for why body_height_norm must also look standing-height.
+        is_confidently_upright = (
+            ext.torso_angle_evidence_quality > 0.0
+            and ext.torso_angle < self.hip_drop_config.upright_torso_angle_threshold
+            and ext.body_height_norm >= self.hip_drop_config.upright_body_height_norm_threshold
+        )
+        self.ctx.update_standing_baseline(base.cog_height, is_confidently_upright)
+
+        scores = self.scorer.score(
+            base, ext, self.base_history, self.ext_history,
+            floor_contact_score=self.floor_contact_score,
+            hip_drop_evidence=hip_drop_evidence,
+        )
+        fusion_result = self.fusion.combine(
+            # cold (0.0) LSTM by default — the whole point of most tests in
+            # this file; some V4.2 tests pass a non-zero value explicitly.
+            lstm_mandown_prob=lstm_mandown_prob,
+            feature_confidence=scores.mandown_confidence,
+            persistence_score=scores.persistence_score,
+            pose_quality=scores.pose_quality_score,
+            down_score=scores.down_score,
+            floor_proximity_score=scores.floor_proximity_score,
+            height_collapse_cue=scores.height_collapse_cue,
+            torso_angle=ext.torso_angle,
+            torso_angle_evidence_quality=ext.torso_angle_evidence_quality,
+        )
+        step_result = self.state_machine.step(fusion_result.suggested_tier)
+        return step_result.state
+
+
+def _bbox_for(keypoints: np.ndarray, pad=20) -> tuple:
+    valid = keypoints[keypoints[:, 2] > 0.3]
+    x1, y1 = valid[:, 0].min() - pad, valid[:, 1].min() - pad
+    x2, y2 = valid[:, 0].max() + pad, valid[:, 1].max() + pad
+    return (float(x1), float(y1), float(x2), float(y2))
+
+
+def _run_static_posture(keypoints_fn, max_frames=40) -> tuple[MandownState, int]:
+    sim = _StaticTrackSimulator()
+    kps = keypoints_fn()
+    bbox = _bbox_for(kps)
+    for frame_num in range(max_frames):
+        state = sim.step(kps, bbox)
+        if state == MandownState.MANDOWN:
+            return state, frame_num
+    return state, max_frames
+
